16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T7b1,The core is a five-stage retrieval-grounded synthesis pipeline split into two phases:
Phase I (Knowledge Extraction, Steps 0-2): 1) A four-level discipline taxonomy: the first three levels (62 L1 / 754 L2 / 2,730 L3 nodes) are adopted from the Chinese National Standard of Discipline Classification; L3 nodes are expanded into 12,657 fine-grained L4 subfields via LLM, followed by LLM-assisted deduplication under each L2 node to cover 15,387 total disciplines. 2) For each leaf discipline, an LLM generates 10-15 statement-form queries covering core concepts, methods, applications, and limitations; statement-form queries are chosen because they match the declarative register of pretraining text and deliver higher cluster retention rates in pilot tests. 3) Each query retrieves the top 100 passages from the pretraining corpus, passages from all queries of the same discipline are aggregated, deduplicated, and clustered into thematic units.
Phase II (Structured Generation, Steps 3-4): 4) Hierarchical tables of contents (TOCs) are planned based on thematic units with quality filtering applied. 5) Source-grounded section content is generated per TOC entry and assembled into complete books, with multi-variant generation across different audiences and writing styles to ensure distributional diversity.
Four controlled settings are designed to isolate variables: Full (retain each TOC-planned textbook as a single training document), Split (use identical generated sections and token budget as Full, but treat each section as an independent document with reset position embeddings and intra-document attention), RandomConcat (randomly concatenate Split sections across books to match Full's length distribution, separating the effect of planned adjacency from raw document length), and Rephrase (independently rewrite individual documents from the same retrieval pool under matched audience/style constraints, without clustering, TOC planning, or book assembly).18:T490,Deep Research Pretraining (DRP) is an offline reverse-synthesis pipeline.
- Inputs: a document corpus plus an evidence graph (citation graph or Wikipedia hyperlink graph).
- Construction: pick a citation-bearing / link-bearing passage as the target report r; recover its evidence set Er (linked/cited documents that substantively support the passage); sample graph-neighborhood alternatives that are related but not selected.
- Proxy objective: infer a research objective u whose answer is expressed by r.
- Rendering: convert (u, evidence, alternatives) into standardized search–open–write trajectories.
- Training objective (predictive navigation): conditioned on the objective and the evidence observed so far, predict what to search, which documents to open, and how to synthesize/write grounded text.
- Key trade-off: no live retrieval environment and no executed policy rollouts; candidate sets and document contents are assembled offline, prioritizing scale and controllability over perfect interaction realism.
- Instantiations: DRP-Paper (citation graphs, Related Work passages) and DRP-Web (Wikipedia hyperlinks with filtering to keep substantive links).19:T446,Setup and reported findings from the provided excerpt:
- Starting point: Qwen3-14B-Base.
- Continual pretraining: 1B tokens on DRP-Paper or DRP-Web.
- Downstream: agent SFT on controlled fractions of 13K GPT-5-generated deep-research trajectories (DR Tulu), measuring performance vs number of expert trajectories.
- Results: consistent gains over no-DRP SFT at low-data budgets on DeepResearch Bench across multiple independently sampled subsets; with 1/4 trajectories, DRP-Web exceeds a fixed full-data Base checkpoint.
- Transfer: improvements carry to ResearchQA, WebWalkerQA, SimpleQA; the 1/16-SFT gain persists on Qwen3-30B-A3B.
- RL continuation: from matched 1/16-SFT checkpoints, DRP-Web stays ahead of Base through 80 steps of ARPO-style agentic RL.
- Controls: source-matched raw-document CPT and evidence-mismatch controls suggest the benefit comes from evidence-conditioned navigation rather than domain exposure or merely imitating agent formatting.
(The excerpt does not include exact score deltas or detailed data composition; those would come from the results tables/appendix.)1a:T788,The method has three stages. First, train a standard byte-level BPE tokenizer as usual and keep the full learned merge tree. There is no modification to the merge-learning objective itself. Second, after training, compute each learned token’s final exposure, meaning how often it actually appears in the fully encoded corpus after all merges are applied. Tokens with low final exposure are marked as internal-only: they remain in the merge tree and can still serve as construction nodes for longer tokens, but they are removed from the model-visible vocabulary. Third, to preserve the target visible vocabulary size, the tokenizer training is resumed beyond the original vocabulary budget, producing additional candidate merges. Better-exposed candidates are then used to fill the visible slots vacated by the pruned tokens.

The encoding design is the key implementation detail. Encoding first follows the full merge rules exactly as in standard BPE. If a resulting token is internal-only, it is recursively expanded into visible child tokens until the returned token sequence contains only visible vocabulary items. This preserves the learned merge structure while changing the model interface. The paper is careful to distinguish this from ordinary vocabulary pruning: the visible vocabulary size is preserved, and the merge tree is not discarded. What changes is which learned tokens are exposed to the LM.

This design is more conservative than simply deleting low-frequency tokens, because it does not break the construction path for longer merges. It is also more controlled than retraining a larger tokenizer and truncating it, because it explicitly separates internal merge nodes from model-visible units. A notable part of the paper is the vocabulary-only evaluation under a shared exact minimum-token objective, intended to isolate the effect of visible vocabulary composition from native BPE merge-order artifacts.1b:T56e,From the provided full-text excerpt, the experimental focus is clearly tokenizer-level evaluation rather than end-to-end large-scale LM pretraining. The paper includes a vocabulary-only evaluation with a shared exact minimum-token objective, which is meant to compare standard BPE and Pruned BPE under the same segmentation target and isolate the effect of visible vocabulary composition. The implementation also supports Unicode-aware pretokenization, language/code-friendly boundaries, CPU-parallel training, sharding, and checkpointing, suggesting experiments likely include multilingual or at least non-Latin-script settings.

The important empirical questions are straightforward: how many learned BPE tokens have low final exposure; whether hiding them as internal-only harms encoded sequence length; whether the replacement tokens have materially better exposure in the final corpus; and whether gains are larger for byte-heavy scripts such as Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. The excerpt does not include the full result tables, so it would be unsafe to invent exact numbers for vocabulary size, threshold settings, token-count changes, or downstream gains. When reading the paper, the critical figures to verify are the exposure distribution, the visible/internal split under different thresholds, the effect on encoded length, and the exact margins in the vocabulary-only evaluation.1c:T5f3,The core premise is a hard utility constraint on rational adversaries: no matter what obfuscation tactics are used, a model that retains expert-level domain performance cannot fully erase intrinsic statistical fingerprints of proprietary data, which sit at the intersection of semantic substance (e.g., domain reasoning logic) and lexical form (e.g., terminological preference). The Distribution Provenance Audit (DPA) framework implements this idea with two components: (1) Joint Semantic-Lexical Similarity (JSLS), a metric that enforces dual matching of semantic consistency and lexical preference, avoiding both the fragility of surface-level lexical metrics to paraphrasing and the inability of pure semantic metrics to distinguish generic domain knowledge from specific proprietary data; (2) Self-Instruct Data Extraction (SIDE), a black-box sampling algorithm that bootstraps from the model's own high-likelihood regions without external prompts, eliminating prompt-induced bias to faithfully reconstruct the model's intrinsic output distribution. The audit is formulated as a formal statistical hypothesis test that compares fingerprints from the extracted model distribution against the proprietary corpus distribution to determine unauthorized data use. The analysis further notes that the same high-fidelity distributional fingerprints enabling audit can be repurposed for distribution-level privacy attacks and data extraction, revealing an inherent structural tradeoff between auditability and privacy leakage.1d:T42f,The framework explicitly decouples duplicate detection from copy retention.
Detection (scalable and shard-invariant): documents are segmented at natural boundaries; each segment is normalized (formatting/casing/whitespace etc., per the paper’s rules) and exact-hashed; distributed key–value aggregation computes global occurrence counts for each hash, ensuring cross-shard visibility.
Retention (explicit policy): instead of keep-one/keep-k, the method defines a retention function k=f(global_frequency, segment_length). High-frequency segments (likely boilerplate/templates) are aggressively compressed; longer repeated spans get smaller budgets as they more often reflect direct copying or templated reuse; low-frequency repeats are treated conservatively to avoid deleting legitimate quotations or mild reuse. A coherence-preserving deletion step reduces fragmentation when removing repeated spans.
Trade-off vs suffix arrays: less coverage for arbitrary cross-boundary substrings, but far better scalability, shard invariance, and controllable retention behavior.1e:T578,The study extends the Hindi vocabulary of Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B. The original tokenizer has 131,072 entries, with only 1,569 entries containing Devanagari characters, about 1.2%. The authors add 25,600 Hindi tokens from the Nanda tokenizer. On 100,000 Sangraha Hindi documents, this reduces Hindi fertility from 1.95 to 1.25 tokens per word.

They compare more than 20 initialization configurations. The design space includes vocabulary averaging baselines, external or learned methods such as FOCUS, top-k semantic retrieval and residual MLP mappings, subword composition, norm calibration, and asymmetric initialization for input embeddings versus the output projection.

The strongest family is subword composition. A new token is tokenized by the old tokenizer, and its vector is initialized from a weighted average of the constituent old-token embeddings. This directly reuses the pretrained embedding geometry, which appears more reliable than projecting from an external semantic space. The best reported configuration uses uniform subword averaging with Hindi-specific norm calibration for the input embedding, and character-length-weighted subword averaging for the output head. A MuRIL-BERT semantic input weighting paired with character-length output weighting performs nearly the same, suggesting that external semantic information can help on the input side but is not the main driver.1f:T675,The core of the work is the OctoLong data pipeline, which combines three components: an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parser, a Language Server Protocol (LSP) backend, and a package manager, to recursively retrieve cross-repository code dependencies. The pipeline works as follows: 1) Curate high-quality Python repositories (≥15 GitHub stars, ≥5 contributors); 2) Use LSP's type- and scope-aware analysis, paired with package manager-resolved dependencies, to recursively fetch implementations of imported classes and functions across repository boundaries; 3) Concatenate these dependencies in call order to form high-density long code contexts up to millions of tokens in length. Two corpora are built from this pipeline: the ~6.2B-token cross-repository long-context code dataset, mixed with other long-text data to form the ~50B-token OctoLong-LCFT corpus for mid-training long-context continued pretraining; and the ~10B-token OctoLong-SFT mix (open instruction data + agent data) for supervised fine-tuning. The training pipeline starts from Qwen3 dense base models (600M to 14B parameters), first performs LCFT to extend the context window to 128K (4x the native length), then runs SFT to produce the OctoLong-Instruct suite. The key difference from prior work: existing cross-document long-context construction relies on weak correlation signals with low context coupling, while single-repository code serialization is limited by repository boundaries. OctoLong achieves precise cross-repository dependency retrieval via LSP, producing tightly coupled multi-hop dependency contexts that scale infinitely with the open-source package ecosystem.20:T41a,Reading priority for deep dive: 1) Section 3 (OctoLong data pipeline): focus on how LSP, AST, and the package manager work together, and the implementation logic of recursive cross-repository dependency retrieval (see Figure 2 for the pipeline flowchart) — this is the core innovation of the paper. 2) Section 4 (training pipeline): focus on the mid-training LCFT recipe details, including data mixture ratio, training steps, and context window configuration, as well as the composition of the SFT dataset. 3) Section 5 (experiments and ablations): focus on two key comparisons — the long-context performance gap between cross-repository code and single-repository code / general long text, and the retention of short-context capabilities after long-context training. 第二步是 identify：作者设计了 controlled fault-source moves 和 always-on module-routed gradient correction。关键点是 source mechanism 仍然开启，只改变哪条模块路径收到 clean fp32 gradient。这样测的是“阻断通道”，不是“修复源头”。结果显示，来自 attention 内部和 attention 外部的误差都会汇聚到同一个 dominant QK channel；纠正 QK route 可以稳定训练，纠正 MLP route 不行。这给出了 source-channel dissociation：fault source is not failure channel。

定位实验区分了 streaming carry 的两类路径。running output O 在 backward 中通过 D-term 影响 score gradient，进而影响 dQ 和 dK，但不直接影响 dV；statistics carry 通过 saved log normalizer 重标定 recomputed probabilities P，会影响 dQ、dK 和 dV。论文借此解释为什么某些 carry precision 会表现为 QK 相关错误，而不是平均地污染所有 attention 参数。

机制实验操纵 error-sign sequences，分离 temporal sign-coherence、per-tile scalar mean 和 aggregate magnitude。只有具有跨 step 符号持续性的误差更容易进入 QK channel。作者也指出它不能直接作为在线触发信号，因为正常 feature learning 也会有时间一致性。QK-Guard 因此选择监控 attention-logit saturation。触发后，per-head QK normalization 能 contain runaway；同一时刻的 softmax-local 处理和 learning-rate cut 失败，支持“必须在 QK locus 动作”的结论。24:T808,The paper follows an isolate-identify-explain-contain structure. First, the authors reproduce a GPT-2-class collapse in a PyTorch implementation of FlashAttention-2's tiled online-softmax recurrence. This implementation exposes the running output O and the softmax statistics carry, which allows controlled precision edits. The decisive intervention is fp32 accumulation in the streaming accumulator: it prevents the reproduced collapse while preserving the tiled computation. This rules out several simpler explanations, including bf16 operands, tiling itself, the FlashAttention family as a whole, or a single-scale artifact.

Second, the authors introduce an identification assay based on controlled fault-source moves and always-on module-routed gradient correction. The source mechanism remains enabled, while clean fp32 gradients are routed through selected modules. This tests channel blocking rather than source repair. The result is the central source-channel dissociation: faults placed inside attention and faults placed outside attention both drive the same dominant QK channel; QK-route correction stabilizes training, while MLP-route correction does not.

Third, the paper explains how errors enter the QK channel. The distinguishing property is temporal sign-coherence: the error sign for a head persists across optimizer steps. This is separated from per-tile scalar mean and total error magnitude. The authors also test causality with equal-energy off-target controls and by removing each run's own dominant QK weight directions, showing that the QK channel drives the early runaway rather than merely tracking it.

Finally, the paper proposes QK-Guard, a dormant containment controller. It monitors attention-logit saturation and, once a runaway is developing, applies parameter-free per-head QK normalization at the QK locus. It does not repair the underlying fault or rewind the run. At the same trigger point, a softmax-local intervention and a learning-rate cut fail, indicating that the rescue depends on where the action is applied.25:T5ef,The empirical base is a bf16 GPT-2 small training setup on OpenWebText. The baseline collapses in every seed within the observed window. In contrast, fp32-accumulation variants do not collapse in the reported runs: two seeds for the accumulator-to-fp32 arm, two seeds for the fp32/fp32 carry condition, and one long run that was manually stopped while still healthy at 103400 logged steps. The paper treats these as sufficiency counterexamples, not as collapse-rate estimates.

The accumulator analysis separates the backward paths of the streaming carries. The running output O re-enters backward through the D-term, perturbing the score gradient and therefore dQ and dK, but not dV. The statistics carry affects recomputed probabilities through the saved log normalizer and can affect dQ, dK, and dV. This explains why a carry-precision fault can show up as a QK-driven instability rather than as uniform attention-parameter noise.

The channel-identification experiments move the fault outside attention and still observe the same QK spectral runaway. With module-routed clean gradients, QK correction blocks the collapse while MLP correction does not. The mechanism experiments manipulate error-sign sequences and show that temporal sign-coherence, rather than scalar mean or aggregate energy, predicts entry into the QK channel. QK-Guard then uses attention-logit saturation as the online signal, because temporal coherence alone is not specific to failure; normal feature learning can also be temporally coherent.26:T51c,Read the introduction carefully for the distinction between fault source, failure channel, trigger signal, and action locus. Section 3 is the key mechanism section. The module-routed gradient correction assay is the central experiment: the fault remains active, but only one route receives a clean gradient. This is what makes the QK-channel conclusion stronger than a standard kernel fix.

The failed softmax-local and learning-rate-cut controls are particularly informative.27:Ta19,方法部分分四步，逻辑很完整。

第一步是定位跨尺寸关系。作者选 Pythia 1.4B→410M 作为主分析对，二者层数和 head 数相同，只缩宽度，因此可以把问题集中在 width transfer。用相同输入序列抽取各层激活后，作者用 ridge regression 拟合大模型表示到小模型表示的线性映射，发现 held-out R^2 达到 0.84，说明表示层面高度线性可对齐。相对地，参数层面对齐很弱，最干净的 embedding 情况也只有 R^2≈0.25–0.39。这一组结果奠定全文主线：函数相近，不代表参数坐标系相近。

第二步是解释为什么稠密权重投影会坏。作者先做了一个很关键的 bit-exact control：从 donor 模型提取权重，再按 head-aware 方式重建模型，logits 完全一致，排除了“权重导出/重组装配错误”的可能。随后分析 dense linear map 的结构性问题。Transformer 里很多子结构不是任意线性基都等价：RoPE 依赖成对维度，attention 依赖 per-head 分块，GELU 是逐元素非线性，LayerNorm 依赖逐特征均值方差。稠密投影把这些坐标混在一起，等于把原本有语义的轴打散。作者还做了分模块破坏分析，指出 LayerNorm 相关结构被破坏带来的影响最大。

第三步是检验“投影后剩下的误差里还有没有可学信号”。作者把最佳线性算子之后的权重残差拿出来，做了谱分析、一致性测试、patch-level learnability、cross-pair transfer，并和 shuffle control 比较。结论是这些残差在统计上和噪声不可区分，bootstrap 置信下 p≥0.99。也就是说，在这个粒度上不存在一个简单的零样本修补器，不能指望再加一个小校正网络就把投影救回来。

第四步是把可转移价值重新定义为初始化问题，并提出 Compensated Selection。这里有两个独立杠杆。其一是 least-squares compensation，对结构保持的子选取权重做闭式最小二乘补偿，目标是让被保留子网络在函数上尽量逼近原模型；它修的是“网络在算什么”。其二是 variance-preserving rescale，对选取后的权重做方差保持缩放，修复优化器看到的尺度，使继续预训练更稳定；它修的是“优化器如何看这些参数”。作者强调这两个杠杆作用在不同权重路径上，因此可以叠加。与 dense projection 不同，这个方法坚持结构保持 selection，而不是任意混基投影；与纯 subcloning 不同，它额外补了函数拟合和训练动态两件事。28:T783,实验设计比较扎实。主对是 Pythia 1.4B→410M：24 层、16 heads 都不变，residual width 2048→1024，head dim 128→64，MLP 8192→4096。这样层一一对应，便于分析。表示对齐用 10,000 条来自 pile-uncopyrighted 的 128-token 序列，前 500 条做 similarity subset，其余用于 mean-pooled 和 last-token 激活统计。评测以 WikiText-103 validation 的 sliding-window perplexity 为主，并补充 C4、2×上下文长度、以及 LAMBADA/ARC-Easy/HellaSwag/PIQA 零样本。

最关键的结果有几组。第一，表示对齐显著强于参数对齐：activation ridge R^2=0.84，而参数 R^2 只有 0.25–0.39。第二，dense projection 的零样本功能几乎崩坏，而且这种崩坏不是 assembly artifact。第三，Compensated Selection 在 matched-budget continued pretraining 中同时赢零样本起点和最终收敛。文中给出的代表数字是：最终 perplexity 84.0±1.8，对比最强 weight subcloning 变体 89.7±3.7；零样本恢复速度上，达到某一质量阈值所需 token 约 18.5k，对比 61.9k。作者还给出一个很直观的样本效率结果：在只继续训练 30M tokens 时，Compensated Selection 相比从头训练完成度高约 18×。在更难设置下，这个优势仍然保留：out-of-domain 的 C4、2×训练上下文长度 2048、以及 held-out 的 depth-dominated 410M→160M 上，排序一致；在后者上，相比 from scratch 仍有约 13× 的优势。另一个扩展实验是 6.9B→1.4B，说明方法不只在单一尺度对上成立。

消融上，作者把 conversion 分成两个独立因素的做法很有信息量：least-squares compensation 提供最好零样本函数恢复，variance-preserving rescale 决定更好的训练终点，二者叠加优于单独使用。这说明“初始化好不好”至少包含函数接近性和优化尺度匹配两个维度，不能只看初始 loss。29:T9cf,The paper proceeds in four steps.

First, it localizes where cross-size similarity lives. The main pair is Pythia 1.4B to 410M, chosen so that depth and head count are unchanged and only width shrinks. Using shared inputs, the authors fit ridge regressions from large-model activations to small-model activations and obtain held-out R^2 of 0.84, indicating strong linear alignment in representation space. In contrast, parameter alignment is weak, with even the clean embedding case only around R^2 = 0.25 to 0.39. This gap drives the rest of the paper.

Second, it diagnoses why dense weight projection is destructive. A key control is bit-exact reconstruction: extracting donor weights and rebuilding the donor reproduces logits exactly, ruling out implementation or assembly artifacts. The failure is therefore in the projection mathematics. A dense linear map mixes bases that are not freely interchangeable in a Transformer. RoPE depends on paired dimensions, attention depends on headwise partitioning, GELU is elementwise, and LayerNorm depends on featurewise statistics. Once these axes are mixed, the projected model no longer respects the computation the architecture expects. The paper further decomposes the damage and finds LayerNorm-related breakage to be the single largest contributor.

Third, it tests whether the residual after the best-fit linear operator contains recoverable structure. The authors analyze residuals with spectral tests, consistency checks, patch-level learnability, and cross-pair transfer, all against shuffle controls. The result is negative: residuals are statistically indistinguishable from noise, with bootstrap comparisons giving p >= 0.99. That rules out a simple zero-shot correction layer at this granularity.

Fourth, it reframes conversion as an initialization problem and proposes Compensated Selection. The method has two independent levers. Least-squares compensation is the function lever: after structure-preserving weight selection, it applies closed-form least-squares corrections so the retained subnetwork better matches the donor’s computation. Variance-preserving rescale is the optimization lever: it restores parameter scale so the optimizer sees a healthy initialization during continued pretraining. These act on disjoint weight paths and therefore stack. This is the key distinction from dense projection, which mixes coordinates, and from plain subcloning, which preserves structure but does not explicitly repair function or optimizer scale.2a:T7c2,The experimental setup is unusually controlled. The main analysis uses Pythia 1.4B to 410M, both with 24 layers and 16 heads, while residual width shrinks from 2048 to 1024, head dimension from 128 to 64, and MLP width from 8192 to 4096. This gives one-to-one layer correspondence and isolates width transfer. Representation analyses use 10,000 shared 128-token sequences from pile-uncopyrighted. Evaluation centers on strided WikiText-103 validation perplexity, with harder checks on C4, 2x context length, and zero-shot tasks including LAMBADA, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, and PIQA.

The main quantitative findings are clear. Representation alignment is strong while parameter alignment is weak: activation ridge R^2 reaches 0.84, whereas parameter R^2 stays around 0.25 to 0.39. Dense projection collapses functionally, and the paper shows this is not due to extraction or reassembly errors. In matched-budget continued pretraining, Compensated Selection beats the strongest weight-subcloning baseline both in zero-shot quality and final endpoint. The headline numbers reported in the paper are final perplexity 84.0 ± 1.8 versus 89.7 ± 3.7, and a much faster recovery trajectory, with 18.5k versus 61.9k tokens to reach the same target quality. At 30M continued-pretraining tokens, the converted initialization is about 18x ahead of training the small model from scratch. The ordering also holds out of domain on C4, at 2x training context, and on a held-out depth-dominated pair, 410M to 160M, where the advantage over scratch remains around 13x. An additional 6.9B to 1.4B experiment suggests the pattern is not unique to one scale pair.

The ablations are especially useful. Least-squares compensation gives the best zero-shot functional recovery, while variance-preserving rescale gives the best final endpoint. Their combination is better than either alone, which is a useful lesson for initialization design: matching function and matching optimization scale are separate problems.2b:T4c0,For a skim, focus on three parts.

Many papers show that dense maps fail; few explain why this cleanly.

If you want the deeper argument, Section 6 is worth reading because it justifies why the authors stop searching for a zero-shot residual corrector and instead treat conversion as initialization only.2c:T56c,The setup is intentionally controlled. Using the official Mamba implementation and the public Muon reference code, the authors compare a pure AdamW baseline against three hybrid assignments: Muon on the input projection group only, Muon on the output projection group only, and Muon on both groups, with all remaining parameters still trained by AdamW. This turns the question into a clean assignment study rather than a noisy optimizer bake-off.

Muon works by applying a fixed-step Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to matrix-valued momentum updates, approximating steepest descent under spectral norm geometry. AdamW, in contrast, is coordinate-wise adaptive. The paper goes beyond loss curves and tracks spectral diagnostics of the affected matrices: condition number, effective rank, and spectral norm. The goal is to test whether any optimization gain is accompanied by systematic spectral changes.

The main technical takeaway is that Muon is not uniformly helpful inside Mamba-2. Applying it only to the output projection group works better than applying it only to the input projection group, and better than applying it to both. The authors also test a natural explanation and reject it: although Muon does reduce the condition number of the matrices it touches, that alone does not explain the validation-loss differences. Functional role matters, not just improved conditioning.2d:T602,The experiments use Mamba-2 130M on OpenWebText and FineWeb-Edu, with token budgets of 1B, 2.6B, and 50B. This is a sensible design because it checks both early token efficiency and behavior well beyond the usual compute-optimal regime, while also testing whether the effect survives across corpora.

The most consistent result is that Muon on the output projection group gives the best outcome among the tested assignments. The gain is primarily in token efficiency: it reaches a given validation loss faster than pure AdamW, rather than dramatically changing the eventual floor. Muon on the input projection is weaker, and applying Muon to both input and output projections does not improve further. That pattern suggests a localized architectural fit rather than a generic optimizer advantage.

The long-budget runs matter. The advantage persists even when training continues far past the nominal compute-optimal point, which makes the result more credible than a short-horizon comparison. On the diagnostic side, Muon systematically lowers the condition number of the matrices it updates and changes their spectral statistics, but those changes do not map cleanly to validation performance. That is an important negative result: cleaner spectra are not sufficient to explain better language-model training.

For pretraining researchers, the useful signal is not a single headline number but the structure of the result: the same optimizer can help one projection group, do little for another, and fail to compose when applied to both.2e:T41d,This is a skim paper, but a careful skim is worthwhile. Start with the parameter-group definitions and the figure showing where the input and output projection groups sit inside the Mamba-2 block. Without that, the optimizer-assignment result feels arbitrary. Then read the main validation-loss comparisons across datasets and token budgets. Focus on whether the ranking of assignments is stable, not on tiny absolute differences.

After that, read the spectral diagnostics. The key point is not that Muon changes condition numbers, but that improved conditioning does not fully account for the training gain. That is where the paper becomes more than a benchmark table.

If time is limited, 20 to 30 minutes is enough to extract the main message: Muon can help Mamba-2, but the benefit is localized to specific projection groups and mostly shows up as token efficiency. If you want a follow-up experiment idea, the obvious next questions are why the output projection is the right target and why applying Muon to both groups fails to compound the gain.2f:T51a,The baseline Sinkhorn matrix optimizer repeatedly normalizes the rows and columns of a matrix gradient and applies a scalar update scale. It is attractive because it removes moment state for dense two-dimensional weights. SAGE-like hybrids typically keep lightweight state for vocabulary tensors and use Sinkhorn for dense matrices. The paper shows that this dense-model role assignment breaks for MoE experts. For expert e, the gradient G_{e,t} is drawn from a changing conditional distribution p(x | e is selected by top-k routing), not from the full minibatch distribution. Since Sinkhorn normalization is nonlinear, Sinkhorn(E[G_t]) and E[Sinkhorn(G_t)] can behave differently. MESH addresses this by maintaining a hidden first-moment signal H_t for expert gradients and applying Sinkhorn to H_t rather than to G_t. Non-expert matrices and vocabulary tensors keep the SAGE/Sinkhorn hybrid treatment. The expert momentum is maintained through the gradient-buffer lifecycle instead of being stored as an explicit optimizer-state tensor. MESH-B adds a coarse block/neuron inverse-RMS multiplier, giving a limited form of adaptive scaling. The paper’s own interpretation is conservative: block-level adaptivity can help, but temporal smoothing before Sinkhorn normalization is the main causal ingredient.30:T43b,Proposes MALT (Muon Augmented by Lightweight Two-sided preconditioning) and its adaptive variant MALTER: 1) Derives a preconditioned Muon formulation based on local quadratic approximation of the loss, using a positive-definite curvature surrogate to construct a transformed space with isotropic quadratic terms, then orthogonalizes preconditioned momentum and maps the direction back to the original parameter space to address both curvature and gradient anisotropy simultaneously; 2) Designs lightweight two-sided diagonal preconditioners: maintains exponential moving averages (EMA) of row-wise and column-wise squared gradient norms to construct left and right diagonal preconditioning matrices, preserving the matrix structure of parameters with minimal extra overhead; 3) Uses norm grafting to stabilize update scale; 4) MALTER further introduces a scalar step size adapted via Adam-style norm-based noise adjustment in the preconditioned space to improve robustness to stochastic gradient noise. Convergence guarantees for stochastic non-convex optimization are also provided.31:T4f7,The model family is based on masked diffusion language modeling. During training, each token is independently replaced by [MASK] according to a noise level t, and a bidirectional Transformer predicts the clean tokens only at masked positions. During generation, the model starts from a fully masked sequence and iteratively denoises it. This differs from AR training in two important ways: supervision is attached to masked positions rather than every next-token conditional, and each prediction conditions on a corrupted full sequence rather than a clean prefix. The MoE layer contains routed experts plus a shared expert. The architecture is parameterized by activation ratio A=(n_a+n_s)/(n_e+n_s), expert granularity G=2d_model/d_expert, and shared-expert ratio S=n_s/(n_a+n_s). The study then performs compute-scaling sweeps: fitting power laws for optimal batch size and learning rate, running IsoFLOP experiments to trade activated model computation against training tokens, and scanning MoE architecture variables to decide how total expert capacity should be decomposed at larger scales. The key methodological point is that scaling decisions are calibrated under the dLLM objective, rather than treating MoE as a drop-in sparse FFN borrowed from AR Transformers.32:T412,Read carefully. Start with the preliminaries to pin down the masked diffusion objective and the A/G/S MoE parameterization. In the IsoFLOP plots, check whether the axis refers to activated compute, token count, or total parameters; otherwise it is easy to confuse capacity growth with per-token compute growth. In the architecture ablations, look for the effect of increasing the expert pool at fixed activated capacity and for the role of shared experts. Read the LLaDA MoE v2 training and evaluation section last, as an extrapolation test of the recipe at the 30B-A3B and 23.5T-token scale. The deeper questions to track are how mask-ratio-dependent supervision changes batch scaling, whether bidirectional corrupted context changes the data-optimal point, and whether the MoE router learns a different specialization pattern under denoising than under AR prediction.33:T49f,The central formulation treats test-time scaling as budgeted inference over the implicit prefix tree of an autoregressive model. Nodes are partial prefixes, complete paths are traces, and an inference algorithm specifies how to expand, score, stop, and aggregate under a budget. The work separates three regimes. Single-trajectory sequential scaling spends extra compute on one evolving solution path. Sampled inference generates completed candidates and then applies voting, reranking, verifier selection, judge selection, or minimum-Bayes-risk style reduction. Partial-state search allocates compute before completion, expanding and pruning unfinished prefixes. A useful distinction is made between evidence computed per trace and decisions made over a completed candidate pool. Causal stopping is modeled separately because it changes generation cost, not just selection behavior. For evaluation, the work distinguishes shared-bank comparisons, which isolate reducers or verifiers on the same candidate pool, from end-to-end comparisons, which evaluate the full inference system. Candidate-bank diagnostics include repeated-sampling metrics that separate discovery from stability.34:T41e,The method is a trace-freeze-fork intervention on native DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The authors first validate deterministic replay of the native reference, then freeze the local MoE state and vary only aggregation semantics. This isolates reduction effects from prompt handling, sampling, router changes, or replay bugs. The paper separates operand representation from accumulator precision through four schemes, P32, C, A, and B, and compares each scheme against a same-mode canonical reference. A and B enumerate reduction orders and map post-mHC states to continuation-text basins. These basins are equivalence classes of executions that yield the same continuation; they are not deployment probabilities. The paper also validates two replay boundaries. Exact reconstruction at the post-mHC endpoint reproduces the measured downstream trajectory within a decode forward. Exact reconstruction of the full persistent state at a decode boundary reproduces the branch across later token boundaries when the next input token is the same naturally generated token.35:T4e6,The native-reference replay check covers 13 prompts. Every replay preserves the reference route trajectory, greedy token sequence, and generated text, with c_moe_max_abs = 0. In a single-layer fork for the “why the sheep” case, A mode enumerates 720 raw permutations and produces 10 distinct continuation texts. B mode maps 720 raw permutations into 360 exact structural classes and produces 11 distinct texts. Every evaluated branch has a post-mHC state different from the native reference: 720/720 for A and 360/360 for B. The direct next-router comparison was disabled in this sweep, so these counts should be read as state-to-text basin compression rather than per-branch route-divergence labels. For one Chinese prompt, the B structural classes split into 202 layoff continuations, 113 hiring continuations, and 45 other continuations. In a 50-prompt exploratory breadth study using maximum-L∞ B-branch selection, cumulative text separation appears in 12, 24, and 36 prompts by horizons of 8, 16, and 32 tokens. The paper also reports that P32, A, and B alter all 192 native-reference route trajectories in the persistent-trajectory comparison, while C is stable over the evaluated states and schedules and preserves native-reference behavior.36:T577,The proposed paradigm, Explorative Modeling (XM), factors the training loop rather than the generation procedure. At each training step, the model explores K candidate latent-to-data matches (operationally: generate K candidates / alignments) and trains on the closest match to the datapoint. The motivation is that in multimodal settings there is no canonical assignment between latents (e.g., noise) and specific datapoints; random pairing forces a single predictor to cover incompatible modes, yielding an average solution (blur in continuous domains, incoherent distributions in discrete domains). By searching for the latent/candidate already closest to each datapoint, different candidates can “commit” to different modes, making mode coverage scale with K (their “generative expressivity”).

They position XM in two regimes: (1) as an add-on to existing generative recipes, where exploration acts like an additional scaling knob improving compute/sample/parameter efficiency; and (2) as a standalone route to strict end-to-end reconstructive generation, where inference can be as little as a single forward pass because the model is trained under the same sampling procedure used at test time.

Mechanistically, the key design choice is the closest-match criterion and how the discrete selection/search is integrated with reconstruction losses so training remains stable and scalable.37:T620,The method, LATCH, has two components. The first is CVC, Confidence-Verified Commit, which decides when the whole sequence may stop. Instead of monitoring a fixed region or using schedule-dependent heuristics, CVC re-extracts and relocates the current candidate answer span at every denoising step. It then requires both high confidence on that span and sustained argmax identity stability across multiple steps. Only when the candidate answer itself has remained stable does the decoder allow a global fill-and-stop. The key change is that the stopping rule verifies the object of interest, the answer candidate, rather than a proxy statistic.

The second component is BWEC, Block-Wise Early Commit, which decides where local commitments may happen during decoding. The authors argue that non-final blocks usually contain intermediate reasoning text, so they can be handled with a cheaper local confidence rule. BWEC therefore applies only to non-final blocks. The final block, and any global termination decision, remains under CVC. This separation is meant to preserve the speed benefits of adaptive sampling while preventing local confidence signals from prematurely freezing the answer region.

A central analytical premise is that candidate stabilization is highly task-dependent. The paper measures stabilization timing with metrics such as s0.9, the decoding progress by which 90% of trajectories have stabilized, and finds a very wide range across tasks. That observation motivates abandoning progress-only early exit in favor of candidate-aware verification.38:T5b0,The evaluation covers 11 tasks and two model families, with LLaDA-8B-Instruct used as the reference decoding backbone and transfer tested to Dream. With one frozen CVC threshold tuple and one fixed BWEC threshold, without per-task or per-model retuning, LATCH achieves 9.3–17.8× speedup on short-answer tasks and 2.0–3.3× on long-reasoning tasks, while staying within a 2.0-point accuracy tolerance relative to full decoding on every task and both model families.

The failure analysis is more informative than the headline speedups. Under a matched free-form zero-shot protocol, Prophet and SchED exceed the 2-point tolerance on all five long-reasoning tasks and both models, with errors as large as 69 points. That strongly suggests the issue is not implementation detail but the level of evidence used for termination. SlowFast, which only adjusts commitment pace, also violates the tolerance on every long-reasoning setting. KLASS remains acceptable only on its calibration backbone and drops by 5–52 points on Dream. The paper uses these results to argue that local commitment heuristics cannot substitute for explicit sequence-level convergence verification.

One notable empirical claim is transferability: the same thresholds work across tasks and model families for LATCH, whereas prior methods do not. That is a meaningful sign that candidate-aware stopping is better aligned with actual convergence behavior than schedule-aware stopping.39:T56f,AURORA-LM fully decouples latent space construction and generative modeling to eliminate conflicting objectives between the two stages. First, a high-capacity text autoencoder is trained independently to produce full-width continuous latent sequences of the same length as the original token sequence, with no sequence downsampling. The autoencoder training objective focuses exclusively on exact text reconstruction, with no added regularization to smooth latents or make them easier to generate, ensuring latents carry all information present in the original text. Second, a diffusion model is tailored to model the distribution of these high-dimensional full-width latents, using a block-causal attention structure: sequences are split into contiguous chunks, with strict causal dependence across chunks (later chunks are generated only after previous chunks are fully determined), while diffusion-based parallel generation operates within each chunk. This design preserves the parallel throughput of diffusion models while maintaining the causal structure required for long-form text coherence, avoiding the long-range logical inconsistencies common to non-causal full-sequence diffusion. At generation time, continuous latents produced by the diffusion model are mapped directly to discrete text via the pretrained autoencoder decoder, with no external reranking or correction required.3a:T485,Evaluations cover unconditional generation, conditional generation, system-level efficiency-quality tradeoffs, and scaling behavior. Key ablation studies examine three core design choices: Latent capacity tests show that sequence downsampling introduces non-trivial reconstruction error and measurable generation quality degradation, confirming full-width uncompressed latents are necessary for high-fidelity text generation. Block size ablations map the tradeoff between speed and coherence: very small blocks regress to token-by-token serial generation with no throughput benefit, while very large blocks break causal structure and degrade long-form coherence. Scaling tests confirm smooth, predictable performance gains as model parameter count and training data volume increase, with no saturation of returns at evaluated scales—a common failure mode of earlier continuous LM designs. System-level comparisons show substantial quality gains over prior compressed-latent continuous diffusion LMs; the block-causal design matches the generation quality of autoregressive baselines while delivering higher throughput via within-block parallel generation.3b:T458,The method starts from the state space duality view of Mamba-2. Under SSD, a selective SSM layer can be interpreted as structured causal attention: the recurrent state behaves like a compressed KV cache, the update writes token-dependent content into the state, and the readout decodes the value needed by the current token. The key observation is that Mamba-2 decodes token-conditioned values from this state, but does not explicitly decode token-conditioned keys. DART adds a state-memory attention branch on top of the Mamba-2 scan. Chunk state contributions produced by the chunked scan are treated as compressed memory slots. The model decodes both keys and values from these state memories, attends to them with the current query, and adds the retrieved state readout back to the Mamba-2 output through a gated residual correction. The design avoids reconstructing a full token-level KV cache, while giving the model a more selective retrieval path than a single recurrent readout. The implementation reuses the Mamba-2 chunked scan and computes the new attention branch with a FlashAttention-style kernel.3c:T44f,PRECOG offline-encodes each document chunk by running the SSM language model over it and capturing per-layer hidden states. At query time, a lightweight embedding index retrieves the best-matching state, which is injected directly as the initial condition of the model's recurrent state. Because the SSM recurrence is time-translation invariant (Δt and B depend only on the current token; A is fixed), the pre-computed state is identical to what the model would reach by ingesting the chunk at the start of the query. The same mechanism fails for Transformers: RoPE or absolute positional encodings make the KV-cache position-entangled, so a pre-computed cache is invalid at other positions; even setting position aside, a Transformer KV-cache for 3000 tokens requires roughly 500× more storage than the SSM hidden state. The paper also proposes SMC (Structured Memory Consolidation), which organizes states from past interactions into a hierarchical persistent memory with cognitive-domain clustering, two-level retrieval, and an adjustable fidelity-storage dial, keeping session initialization O(1).3d:T523,The analysis starts from the per-head ALiBi logit form A_{i,j} - m_h D_{i,j}, where m_h is the slope and D_{i,j} is token distance. When this value falls below the representable exponential threshold, the softmax numerator becomes exactly zero. The paper reports thresholds of approximately -103.27 for fp32 and -92.18 for bf16. Because the distance term grows without bound, every positive slope will eventually underflow; larger slopes fail earlier, while flatter slopes fail later. The authors formalize the corresponding blindness distance and separate two effects: positional blindness, where distant values cannot contribute to the head output, and weight redistribution, where zeroed terms disappear from the softmax denominator. The mitigation study considers training-time changes to the bias: clamping the bias before underflow, choosing slope schedules matched to the target context length, replacing linear distance with logarithmic or otherwise sublinear distance scaling, and evaluating combinations of these choices. The trade-off is clear: clamping prevents zero weights but collapses distance resolution beyond the clamp; smaller slopes delay failure but do not remove the linear-growth issue; logarithmic distances reduce underflow pressure but change the positional prior learned during training.3e:T4b6,MDLMPE explicitly conditions positional representations on the denoising state. It starts from a binary availability sequence indicating which positions contain revealed tokens and which positions are masked or attention-invalid. For each target token, a target-centered Gaussian weighting is applied to represent the spatial distribution of visible evidence around that token. For an attention pair, the two centered views are averaged into a joint distribution, so the attention relation can depend on both relative distance and the surrounding availability pattern.

The distribution is then projected through a cosine basis to produce features. The method injects these features through two paths. Token-level features are added to the token representation. Pair-level features are mapped by a lightweight MLP into angular offsets for RoPE. This keeps the relative-position geometry of RoPE, but makes the rotations responsive to the current mask pattern. The method is different from long-context RoPE adaptations such as LongLLaDA and UltraLLaDA, which mainly target extrapolation beyond the pretraining length; MDLMPE targets the changing availability topology within the current denoising sequence.3f:T87a,Maglev 由两个耦合模型组成：prefiller Q 和 decoder P。

Q 是训练时使用的强模型。它是因果的，但拥有比部署模型更强的上下文访问能力。文中实际实现里，Q 使用 interleaved full attention 和 sliding-window attention，因此它能在不看未来的前提下，用整段已观测前缀并行地产生每个位置的目标记忆 m'_t。这里的关键不是 Q 的具体形式，而是它必须比 P 更有表达力，能给出一个“理想记忆轨迹”。

P 是真正部署的模型。它只使用 sliding-window attention，再加一个 recurrent K/V injection 通道，把前一时刻或前一段的 memory window 作为额外 K/V 输入。P 在位置 t 既要预测下一个 token，也要输出自己的记忆 m_t。作者把 decoder 最后一层的 normalized state 同时作为 LM head 输入和 memory 写入值，因此不需要额外 memory token，也不需要单独的 memory cache 结构。推理时，P 只保留固定大小的 token window 和 memory window，随着序列增长成本不再增加。

训练难点在于：如果直接训练 P 的递归接口，就必须顺序生成 m_1, m_2, ..., m_T，失去 Transformer 预训练最重要的序列并行性。作者的 lifted parallel training 通过 Q 绕开这个问题。训练时先用 Q 在整段序列上并行生成 m'_1:T，再把移位后的 m'_{0:T-1} 喂给 P，让 P 在并行条件下学习两件事：一是用这些目标记忆做 next-token prediction，二是输出自己的 m_t 去逼近 m'_t。这个 consistency loss 把“内部状态监督”显式化了。到推理时，Q 被丢弃，P 用自己上一时刻生成的 memory 闭环运行。

从方法取舍看，Maglev 和 segment-level memory Transformer 的区别在于它是 token-wise memory，没有块边界；和 linear attention/SSM 的区别在于 memory update 经过完整 Transformer 深度，是非线性的；和普通 sliding-window Transformer 的区别在于它多了一个可持续的 latent memory 通道；和直接训练 recurrent Transformer 的区别在于它把训练中的 latent trajectory 外显出来，用双通路并行训练替代顺序展开。40:T885,Maglev consists of two coupled models, a prefiller Q and a decoder P.

Q is used only during training. It is causal, but more expressive than the deployed model because it has access to a larger receptive field. In the implementation described in the paper, Q uses interleaved full attention and sliding-window attention. Its job is to produce a target memory trajectory m'_1:T in parallel from the observed prefix, without leaking future information.

P is the deployed model. It uses sliding-window attention plus recurrent K/V injection, where a shifted memory window is inserted as additional key-value context. At each position, P predicts the next token and emits its own memory m_t. A notable design choice is that the decoder’s final normalized state serves both as the input to the LM head and as the written memory. This avoids dedicated memory tokens and avoids a separate memory-cache mechanism. At inference time, P keeps only a fixed token window and a fixed memory window, so cost remains bounded as the sequence grows.

The training challenge is that direct recurrent training would require sequentially generating m_1, m_2, ..., m_T, which destroys the sequence parallelism that makes Transformer pretraining efficient. The paper’s lifted parallel training avoids this by externalizing the latent trajectory. First, Q computes m'_1:T in a causal but sequence-parallel pass. Then shifted memories m'_{0:T-1} are fed into P, which is trained in parallel to do two things: predict next tokens and reproduce the target memories via a consistency loss between m_t and m'_t. At inference, Q is discarded and P closes the loop with its own generated memories.

Relative to prior approaches, Maglev differs from segment-level memory Transformers by writing memory at every token rather than at block boundaries. It differs from linear attention and SSMs by using full nonlinear Transformer depth for each memory update. It differs from a plain sliding-window Transformer by adding a persistent latent-memory channel. And it differs from directly trained recurrent Transformers by replacing sequential latent-state unrolling with a two-pass parallel training procedure.41:T62a,The headline experiment uses a deployed decoder at roughly 435M parameters trained on 43.52B tokens. The main baselines are a matched sliding-window Transformer and a matched latent recurrent Transformer. The key reported result is on FineWeb-Edu validation BPB, improving from 0.7413 to 0.7251. Average downstream accuracy improves from 54.1 to 56.4. The gains are moderate rather than dramatic, but they are meaningful given matched model scale and training budget, and they suggest that bounded recurrent memory can improve language modeling beyond what a plain sliding window captures.

Two additional experimental points are especially relevant. First, Q and P can share most parameters while retaining most of the gains. This matters because otherwise the training setup would look like nearly doubling the model. Parameter sharing makes the recipe more plausible for large-scale pretraining. Second, Maglev outperforms not only the sliding-window baseline but also a matched latent recurrent Transformer baseline, which suggests the benefit is not merely from adding state, but from the specific target-memory construction and consistency-training interface.

When reading the experiments, the most informative ablations are likely to be memory-window size, prefiller strength, and consistency-loss weighting. These determine whether the gains come from a genuinely stable recurrent interface or simply from a stronger training-time teacher. Another important axis is the amount of parameter sharing between Q and P, since that directly affects the true pretraining cost.42:T4a8,A useful skim is to read it in the order of problem, interface, and cost.

Start with the introduction and the main architecture figure. The paper is not primarily about making attention cheaper. It is about making token-wise latent memory trainable in parallel. Once that is clear, the Q/P split makes sense.

Then read the method section carefully, especially the definition of lifted parallel training. Three details matter: whether the prefiller memories are strictly causal, exactly what inputs the decoder receives during training, and where the consistency loss is applied. These determine the degree of train-test mismatch and whether the recurrent interface is likely to remain stable at deployment.

Finally, read the main results and ablations. Prioritize comparisons against the matched sliding-window Transformer, the matched latent recurrent baseline, and the parameter-sharing variants. A solid skim should take about 30 to 45 minutes. If the goal is to judge relevance for foundation-model pretraining, look more closely at throughput, memory overhead, whether the prefiller still relies on full attention, and whether memory drift accumulates during long recurrent inference.43:T759,The model continues the Kathleen line. The input side uses a ByteRotate encoder: instead of learning 256 separate byte embeddings, it learns one vector and derives all byte representations through DFT phase rotation. This means the whole byte alphabet is covered with only 128 parameters. Sequence modeling is handled by a multi-scale reverberant state, which replaces attention with three banks of content-gated exponential decay states. The recurrence is s_t = gamma_t s_{t-1} + (1-gamma_t) v_t, where gamma_t depends on content, and the three decay ranges cover short, medium, and long memory. A reverb block is LayerNorm, then reverb in parallel with causal depthwise convolution, then learned gate mixing, then FFN. The trunk has three such blocks with hidden size 128. A notable engineering addition is fast scan: the recurrence is parallelized in chunks of 16 using a cumprod/cumsum closed form, numerically matching the sequential loop to 1e-7 while giving roughly 10–50x wall-clock speedup. That makes the 512 MB training point feasible on free-tier hardware. The baseline is a parameter-matched attention model with the same skeleton, replacing reverb plus convolution by 4-head causal SDPA. Beyond byte-level LM, the paper also uses a 3.08M-parameter word-level variant with a 10K vocabulary for generation studies. Another technical contribution is FORM DISTANCE, a non-parametric, frozen, offline metric for whether sampled text has the statistical form of natural text. It is not a semantic metric. The authors explicitly document one case where the metric was gamed and how they patched it, which makes the evaluation setup more credible than LLM-as-a-judge for this setting. Finally, the decode-time attribution study compares decoding policies, retrieved phrase memory, and several trunk modifications to isolate where generation improvements actually come from.44:T64b,The central experiment is a five-point data-scaling study on WikiText-103 raw UTF-8 bytes, using training subsets of 2, 8, 32, 128, and 512 MB, a fixed 1 MB test slice, 2 epochs, sequence length 256 bytes, and identical AdamW plus cosine recipes for both models. The attention-free reverb model wins at every data point against the parameter-matched transformer baseline. At 512 MB, the reverb model reaches 1.84 bits per byte versus 2.04 for the transformer. At 32 MB, reverb gets 2.011 bpb, while the transformer trained on the full 512 MB still only reaches 2.043 bpb, which the authors summarize as at least a 16x data advantage at equal scale. The log-log slopes are -0.074 for REVERB and -0.107 for ATTN. The paper correctly warns against reading the steeper transformer slope as superiority; it is more consistent with catching up from behind, while both curves are already flattening. Model sizes are 565,888 parameters for the byte-level reverb LM and 463,360 for the attention baseline. The paper also reports replication on a second dataset and a frozen-probe transfer study that supports the same conclusion. The generation-side result is arguably more interesting: at this small scale, text form is driven mainly by decoding policy and retrieved phrases, not by extra architectural additions to the trunk. Four pre-registered trunk additions did not help. That negative result is useful. The main caveat is scope: the advantage is shown in a byte-level, tiny-model, low-budget regime, and should not be read as evidence that attention-free models will dominate at medium or large pretraining scale.45:T491,A good skim follows the question structure. Start with the architecture section to understand exactly what ByteRotate and multi-scale reverb replace, and what inductive bias they introduce. Then read the scaling section carefully, focusing on fairness of parameter matching, identical training recipes, and the full bpb curves rather than a single endpoint. After that, read the FORM DISTANCE section, including the validation and the patch after metric gaming; this part is easy to overlook, but it shows unusual care in generation evaluation. Finish with the decode-time attribution study, especially which trunk modifications failed and which decoding or retrieval settings helped. About 30 minutes should be enough to capture the main message. For a deeper read, Appendix A on fast scan is worth attention because engineering feasibility is central if this family is ever to be tested at larger scale. Two questions should stay in mind while reading: whether the data-efficiency gain partly reflects asymmetry between byte-level modeling and the chosen attention baseline, and whether FORM DISTANCE measures only textual form rather than general generation quality.46:T5f6,SpecDrop is intentionally simple. The model has a shared stem, K parallel modules, and a shared head. Categories are assigned to modules through a fixed assignment matrix, implemented in the simplest case by round-robin mapping from M categories to K modules. During training, for an example with category c, the assigned module is kept with high probability p_a, while all other modules are kept with a small leakage probability p_i. So this is not hard routing; some cross-category gradient sharing remains. The branch outputs are merged using a category-independent fixed denominator S. The paper argues that this denominator makes train and test forward passes match in expectation and keeps the merged activation scale calibrated to the single-branch scale, avoiding magnitude drift from stochastic dropout. An optional always-on shared expert can capture general features. There are no learned routing parameters and no auxiliary load-balancing losses. The point is not that fixed routing is universally better than learned routing. The point is to isolate the variable: if a minimal parameter-free routing scheme already works on clean partitions and fails on fuzzy ones, then the bottleneck is likely partition alignment rather than router design. A strong part of the paper is the information-matched masking control, where the same category label is given to a dense model through output masking. This separates the value of label information itself from the value of turning that information into modular structure.47:T4bb,The experiments span four settings across vision and language. The strongest positive results appear in aligned vision partitions. On CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K with superclass labels, SpecDrop clearly outperforms parameter-matched baselines that do not use the category label. The abstract reports +4.75 top-1 over dense on CIFAR-100 and +6.53 over matched No-Routing+SE on ImageNet-1K, while also leading the multi-branch routing baselines evaluated by the authors. At the same time, the information-matched masking control shows that if the only goal is accuracy, directly using the label to mask a dense model can be even stronger. SpecDrop’s contribution is therefore not superior label usage per se, but the induction of trained modular structure. The language results are the more important constraint. On fuzzy partitions in SlimPajama-6B language modeling and SuperNI/LoRA instruction tuning over Llama-3.2-1B, SpecDrop is essentially tied with matched-architecture baselines within seed noise. That negative result is central: it limits how far the method can be extrapolated to LLM pretraining and supports the paper’s claim that partition clarity, not router complexity, is the binding condition.48:T6d9,实验覆盖三类模型：Mistral-7B、Qwen3-8B、Llama-3.1-8B。SOP canary 预注册为 24 个 SOP × 3 个随机种子，共 144 个 paired events per arm，并按 seed 报告。验收 guard 包括 WikiText-2 perplexity、MMLU 0-shot，以及 data-free output-fidelity probe。

关键结果很清楚。Mistral-7B 上，一个 in-regime 的 SVD build 只有 1.069× baseline perplexity，仍在常见 1.15× 接受带内，但相对原模型每个 query 多编造 +1.729 个步骤，95% CI 为 [1.076, 2.424]，三个 seed 分别是 2.06/1.90/1.85。与之匹配 perplexity 的 magnitude pruning build invention 为 -0.146，CI [-0.375, +0.035]，基本在 0 附近。Qwen3-8B 上，1.17× perplexity 的 SVD build invention 为 +0.208 [0.042, 0.375]，而 damage-matched prune 为 0.000 [0, 0]。Llama-3.1-8B 上，在 ppl 1.29× 时，SVD invention 为 +1.285 [0.743, 1.882]，而 pruning 仅 +0.069 [0.021, 0.125]，差距约 18×。

论文还给出一个很强的 dissociation：同一组 Qwen3-8B 的 probe-allocated b98 SVD 权重，在 paired fidelity test 上显著优于对照，但在 canary 上却显著失败，invention 为 +0.643 [0.171, 1.229]。也就是说，fidelity-up 和 behavior-broken 可以在同一组 tensor 上同时成立。

机制分析部分的结论也值得记住：量化在中等剂量下即便 raw perplexity 损伤更大，也未必触发 canary；但当量化被推到与失败 SVD cell 相近的 error rate，例如 1.05×，也会失败，pooled clean-slice Δ 为 +0.10 [0.029, 0.20]。作者据此认为，触发因素是误差相干性乘以错误率，而不是单纯的 perplexity 损伤。并且 onset 很早，在约 2% perplexity dose 内就能出现，说明这是分布式而非局部层的效应。49:T746,The work has three main components. First, it builds a canary task for procedure execution. Each synthetic SOP contains 10 ordered steps plus a conditional 11th step. The prompt includes both a target SOP and a distractor SOP, and the model must enumerate the exact ordered steps under two paraphrased conditions. Evaluation includes step recall and branch correctness, but the key metric is invented_x: the number of step strings drawn from the global SOP vocabulary that do not belong to the target SOP or its own conditional branch. This isolates fabricated procedure content rather than generic recall errors.

Second, the paper compares compression operators at matched perplexity dose. It contrasts coherent low-rank truncation, implemented as per-tensor SVD truncation, with magnitude pruning, and uses quantization as an additional control. The design is important: by matching perplexity as closely as possible, the authors try to hold overall damage constant and test whether behavior still differs by operator. Their central finding is that coherent low-rank error induces procedure invention while pruning at similar perplexity often does not. This leads to the mechanism claim that the relevant axis is coherence times rate, not damage magnitude alone.

Third, the paper proposes a cheap data-free detector, a two-axis coherence screen, to predict which compressed builds will fail the canary. The exact implementation details are not fully visible from the provided text, but it is described as a fixed-threshold pre-flight check operating across architectures without labeled safety data. The authors are careful to say that the fidelity probe itself is not the main claim; the stronger point is the dissociation between fidelity and safe agentic behavior, and then the conversion of that cautionary result into a more actionable screening method.4a:T72f,The experiments cover three model families: Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B. The SOP canary is pre-registered with 24 SOPs and 3 random seeds, giving 144 paired events per arm, with seed-level reporting. The standard acceptance guards are WikiText-2 perplexity, zero-shot MMLU, and a data-free output-fidelity probe.

The main quantitative results are sharp. On Mistral-7B, an in-regime SVD build at only 1.069× baseline perplexity, comfortably inside the common 1.15× acceptance band, produces +1.729 invented steps per query over baseline, with a 95% CI of [1.076, 2.424]. The three seeds are consistently high at 2.06, 1.90, and 1.85. A magnitude-pruned build matched to the same perplexity gives -0.146 with CI [-0.375, +0.035], effectively near zero. On Qwen3-8B, an SVD build at 1.17× perplexity yields +0.208 [0.042, 0.375], while the damage-matched prune arm is exactly 0.000 [0, 0]. On Llama-3.1-8B, at 1.29× perplexity, SVD gives +1.285 [0.743, 1.882] whereas pruning gives only +0.069 [0.021, 0.125], an 18× gap.

A particularly strong dissociation appears within a single Qwen3-8B arm. The probe-allocated b98 SVD build wins a paired output-fidelity test and still fails the canary with +0.643 invented steps [0.171, 1.229]. So fidelity-up and behavior-broken can hold on the same tensors.

The mechanism section adds an important control. Moderate quantization can carry more raw perplexity damage than the failing SVD dose and still pass the canary, but when quantization is pushed to a similar error rate, around 1.05×, it also fails, with pooled clean-slice Δ of +0.10 [0.029, 0.20]. The authors therefore argue that the trigger is coherence times rate rather than perplexity damage alone. They also note that onset is early, within roughly a 2% perplexity dose, and appears distributed rather than localized.4b:T47c,For a skim, start with the blind-spot and dissociation section. Pay close attention to how invented_x is defined and why the paired SOP setup is diagnostic. That is the strongest part of the paper. Then read the mechanism section, especially the matched-perplexity comparisons among SVD, pruning, and quantization. The phrase 'coherence × rate, not damage' is the central interpretive claim, and it is worth checking whether the controls support it. For anyone working on compression or deployment, the main takeaway is not a single detector but a stricter acceptance logic: passing ppl, MMLU, and fidelity does not certify safe agentic execution.4c:T881,WIDE 的方法可以拆成‘路由学习’和‘执行实现’两部分。

先看路由学习。作者做的是 token-wise dynamic width pruning：每个 token 在每一层都可以独立选择保留哪些 attention head groups 和哪些 FFN channel groups，而不是像已有动态方法那样只决定“这一层算不算”或“这一整个子模块跳不跳”。为了让这种选择既细粒度又不至于完全失去结构性，attention 侧按 GQA 对齐的 head groups 做选择，FFN 侧按可配置 channel groups 做选择。group size 是一个显式超参，控制灵活性与 kernel 效率的折中：组越小，路由越细；组越大，执行越规整。路由器本身是轻量 bottleneck router，并采用 differentiable router-only calibration，也就是主要训练路由决策而不大改主干权重；必要时再加一个可选的 LoRA recovery 来补回精度。这个 recipe 的好处是部署改动小、校准成本低，也避免了全模型重训。

再看执行实现。论文认为细粒度动态稀疏落不了地，主要卡在两个点：一是同步的 mask-to-index 转换开销，二是 token-specific gather/scatter 导致的执行不规则。WIDE 的解法是先做 mask reordering，把任意 token-wise routing pattern 重排成更规则的执行布局：同一 routing group 的 active tokens 被 pack 到 tile-aligned prefix 中。这样原本稀疏且离散的 token 分布，被转成更适合 GPU block/CTA 处理的局部连续布局。在此基础上，作者设计了多级 predication kernel：先用 hardware-agnostic predicate 跳过完全 inactive 的 CTA，再用 architecture-aware predicate 进一步跳过 inactive 的 memory packet 和 tensor-core fragment。也就是说，它不是简单把稀疏张量喂给通用 kernel，而是围绕动态宽度掩码重新组织数据流和计算流。

与已有动态深度剪枝相比，WIDE 的区别不只是粒度更细，还在于它把‘粒度设计’和‘kernel 形状’绑在一起。很多动态方法在论文里默认稀疏就会带来加速，但 WIDE 明确承认不规则性会吞掉收益，因此把重排和 predication 作为一等公民。4d:T7a6,The method has two tightly coupled parts: routing and execution.

On the routing side, WIDE performs token-wise dynamic width pruning. For each token at each layer, lightweight bottleneck routers select which attention-head groups and which FFN-channel groups remain active. This is finer than prior dynamic pruning methods that decide whether to execute or skip an entire layer or submodule. To preserve structure, attention groups are aligned with GQA groups, and FFN channels are partitioned into configurable groups. Group size is a key control knob: smaller groups give more flexibility, larger groups improve kernel regularity. Training is done through differentiable router-only calibration, so the backbone is minimally modified; an optional LoRA recovery stage can restore quality if needed.

On the execution side, the paper identifies two main bottlenecks that prevent fine-grained dynamic sparsity from yielding real speedups: synchronized mask-to-index conversion and irregular gather/scatter patterns. WIDE introduces mask reordering to transform arbitrary token-wise routing masks into a more structured execution layout. Active tokens for each routing group are packed into tile-aligned prefixes, which converts irregular sparsity into CTA-friendly regularity. Based on that layout, the kernels apply multi-stage predication: hardware-agnostic predicates skip fully inactive CTAs, while architecture-aware predicates further avoid inactive memory-loading packets and tensor-core fragments. In other words, WIDE does not simply feed sparse tensors into generic kernels; it reorganizes both data layout and compute scheduling around dynamic width masks.

What differentiates WIDE from prior dynamic depth pruning is not only finer granularity, but the explicit co-design between pruning pattern and kernel structure. The paper directly addresses the usual failure mode of dynamic sparsity: theoretical savings being eaten by execution overhead.4e:T5e5,From the provided content, the experimental story is clear even if not all numbers are visible here. The paper evaluates both prefill and decoding, and reports end-to-end acceleration rather than only kernel-level microbenchmarks. It compares against static structured pruning and prior dynamic sparsity baselines. The claimed outcome is a better quality-efficiency Pareto frontier: token-wise width allocation retains more useful capacity than coarse layer skipping, while the custom kernels allow a larger fraction of theoretical compute savings to become actual runtime gains.

The most important quantitative details to extract from the full paper are likely: model sizes and backbones used for evaluation; quality drop versus throughput gain under different sparsity targets; whether prefill and decode benefit similarly; and how much optional LoRA recovery helps beyond router-only calibration. Those numbers determine whether the method is mainly a systems win, mainly an algorithmic win, or genuinely both.

For ablations, the most informative ones should be: dynamic width pruning without the specialized kernels; the isolated effect of mask reordering; separate contributions from attention-group pruning and FFN-group pruning; and the trade-off curve as group size varies. These analyses answer the central question of the paper: whether the gain comes mostly from better adaptive sparsity patterns or from better execution engineering. If both are necessary, that is exactly the point of the work.4f:T479,For a quick read, follow two threads. First, understand why existing dynamic pruning often fails to deliver practical speedups. In BF16, replicas are exact, which means each execution contract is stable. Yet live-cache continuation and one-shot-prefill continuation disagree on 166 suffixes and on 20 correctness labels. The result identifies the full KV cache as a sufficient carrier of the observed suffix differences, without claiming a universal BF16 rule or a specific kernel-level cause.51:T475,1) Aggregate final scores show no statistically significant quantization gap after multiple-comparison correction; the largest 2.0-point gap is only 1.3× run-to-run noise, creating a false lossless appearance. 2) Per-step decomposition reveals quantization does not alter failure mode sets (0.97 correlation between BF16 and INT4 hallucinated tool names, only 0.18% novel errors) but amplifies frequency: 1× to 4.6× across cells, with Gemma-4 dense in telecom showing 2.5× more out-of-list calls (649 → 1,646). 3) Error budget masking is verified: tightening allowed failed calls from 10 to 2 per episode widens the INT4 gap from 1.3 to 16.7 points, with the full 15.4-point significant gap localized exclusively to the high-amplification cell (max 0.2 points elsewhere); a targeted repair prompt only improves scores in that cell. 4) Damage is gated by full-precision failure propensity, not size or architecture: Qwen-3.6 with rare BF16 hallucinations shows no amplification, while Gemma-4 with inherent hallucination tendency is significantly amplified, consistent with quantization noise only flipping thin-margin argmax decisions.52:T76d,The method has two main components: Mixture-of-Translators (MoT) and a Context Correction Loss.

The setup is straightforward. Given a source model MSrc and its context cache KVSrc,Ctx for a long context xCtx, the goal is to produce a translated cache \hat{KV}Tgt,Ctx that a target model can continue from, ideally behaving similarly to the target model’s own native prefill on the same context. The challenge is that source and target models may differ substantially in architecture, so a simple one-shot projection is often too rigid.

MoT addresses this by using multiple translator modules instead of a single universal translator. A gating mechanism combines them, effectively allowing token-level or state-level mixtures of translation modes. The underlying claim is sensible: heterogeneous source–target mappings are not uniform. Different tokens or subspaces may require different translation behaviors, so a mixture can model local correspondences better than one global path or one shared latent space.

The paper also identifies two competing error sources:
1. Propagation error: if translation happens too early, translation noise is propagated and amplified through the remaining target layers.
2. Correction-deficit error: if translation happens too late, the target model has too few upper layers left to repair the mismatch.

This explains the reported U-shaped validation loss as a function of translation depth. MoT mainly attacks the first issue by increasing translation capacity. The Context Correction Loss addresses the second by supervising the replayed target-side trajectory after translation to match the native target trajectory. This is more meaningful than static feature matching alone, because what matters for generation is not just whether translated caches look similar in isolation, but whether they evolve similarly once the target model continues computation.53:T616,The evaluation covers closed-set QA, extractive QA, multi-agent reasoning, and long-context cache-augmented generation, using both homogeneous and heterogeneous source–target pairs among Qwen2.5, GPT-2, and OPT.

The key reported numbers from the provided text are:
1. At the Qwen2.5-7B scale, MoT achieves 51.0% average accuracy on closed-set QA and 0.43 average F1 on extractive QA.
2. In GPT-family experiments, it reaches 42.0% average accuracy and 0.22 average F1.
3. In long-context cache-augmented generation, MoT preserves 96.3% of direct-context quality, suggesting that translated caches retain most of the information needed for downstream generation.
4. In the 10-agent setting, Figure 2 shows that MoT maintains F1 while reducing peak GPU memory by more than 1 GiB, and the authors describe this as scale-invariant memory behavior because context memory does not need to grow linearly with the number of agents.

One of the more informative analyses varies the first translated layer and finds a U-shaped validation-loss curve. The paper also shows that last-state shift decays exponentially with layer position. Together, these results support the proposed two-error explanation rather than leaving it as an intuition.

For a careful reading, three questions remain important: how close these translated-cache results are to the native target upper bound, which heterogeneous pairs are hardest to translate, and whether translator training cost offsets part of the runtime benefit.
