Fewer than 2% of calls fail to produce a parseable score on the first attempt, and only four off-bucket scores appear across all runs.8a:T53f,AgentMemBench implements five memory families under one harness. ICW keeps only a recent in-context window. EKV stores conversation snippets in an external key-value memory and retrieves them by dense similarity. GEM extracts entities and relations into an episodic knowledge graph, then retrieves structured neighborhoods. CBS compresses older context into natural-language summaries. WAM augments the agent with external web or MCP-style tool access. The benchmark uses three public datasets: 200 question turns from LoCoMo, 187 from MultiDoc2Dial, and 104 from MSC, for 491 annotated question turns in total. This yields 15 main configurations across five strategies and three task types. The metrics cover retrieval quality, including Memory Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG@k; answer quality, including Answer F1 and an LLM-judge faithfulness score; and deployment efficiency, including memory footprint, token cost, and latency. A notable design choice is provenance-aware retrieval evaluation: retrieved items carry true session/turn provenance, so retrieval metrics are computed against gold-session annotations rather than against ad-hoc retrieval indices. The paper also evaluates MemGPT/Letta and HippoRAG in the same harness and introduces MADS, a zero-shot dynamic selector that chooses a memory strategy from four corpus-level statistics.8b:T402,OpenART builds executable environments from validated dependency graphs synthesized from more than 500K Tools, MCPs, and Skills. Each scenario combines a benign task objective with a hidden safety contract and is admitted only after deterministic evaluator checks and automated behavioral probes. The scenario representation is target-agnostic until execution. Lightweight adapters then project the same task, contract, and evaluator into each agent’s native interface. The exposed attack surfaces include workspace, instructions, Skills, Tools, MCPs, short-term memory, plan state, and long-term memory. The reference attack policy, EMHA, formulates environment evolution as black-box optimization over a Markov hypergraph. It uses evaluator feedback to refine future state transitions without updating model parameters. A key design choice is that only target-visible environment state evolves; the benign task and hidden safety contract stay unchanged, which makes comparisons across agents and complexity levels cleaner.8c:T68f,The pipeline has three stages. First, CoT trajectory generation: for each question, a teacher LLM produces a zero-shot chain-of-thought trajectory. The key premise is that questions with different wording but similar logical structure become closer once their reasoning paths are made explicit. Second, contextualized trajectory embedding: the question and its generated reasoning trace are embedded into a dense space intended to reflect the latent reasoning manifold better than plain question embeddings. Third, isomorphic clustering and selection: clustering or geometric covering is performed in that space, and representative items near cluster centers are selected under a fixed budget.

A useful design choice is the decoupling between subset selection and score estimation. CoT-Core only constructs the subset. The selected coreset can be used with simple standard aggregation in a fully training-free setup, or combined with stronger estimators such as GP-IRT when historical logs are available. This is more flexible than IRT-style methods, which typically tie item calibration and score reconstruction together.

Compared with lexical embedding plus k-center selection, the novelty is not the sampler itself but the representation space: neighborhood structure is induced by generated reasoning traces rather than surface wording. Compared with IRT-based approaches, it avoids the cold-start dependency on historical correctness matrices. The trade-off is also clear: it is training-free, but not cost-free, because CoT trajectories must be generated for the benchmark upfront. The method assumes that this one-time cost is amortized over many future evaluation runs.8d:T58c,The experimental section is organized around three questions: whether CoT-based representations are better than plain text embeddings for coreset construction, whether the selected subsets remain faithful in cold-start score estimation, and when the gains disappear.

The paper compares against two baseline families: history-dependent approaches such as IRT/GP-IRT, and training-free geometric methods based on question embeddings, including k-center-style selection. The main result is that in cold-start settings, CoT-Core consistently outperforms text-only selection, especially on benchmarks with nontrivial multi-step reasoning. The selected subsets better preserve full-benchmark score estimates and model ranking. The paper also states a boundary condition: when tasks are dominated by factual recall, template matching, or shallow judgments, the benefit of reasoning-aware pruning becomes smaller because the underlying reasoning manifold is weak to begin with.

The most informative ablations vary the use of CoT, the embedding construction, the clustering/selection strategy, and the downstream estimator. The main takeaway is that the gain comes primarily from the reasoning-aware representation rather than from a particular clustering heuristic. The provided content does not expose complete tables or reliable numeric values, so it would be inappropriate to invent exact percentages or correlation scores.8e:T426,A minimal Turing-complete tape automaton F (Brainfuck family, five instructions) is fixed, and all ~1.5 billion programs of length L≤13 are exhaustively enumerated under a bounded universal (Levin–Solomonoff) prior. Because enumeration is exact, the map from program behavior to prior mass is a sufficient statistic, and the posterior predictive for any few-shot context is computed in closed form. To remove output-polarity bias, F is complement-symmetrized into sF; each task is paired with its bitwise complement twin, on which the optimum scores identically, so the original-twin gap isolates the model's own inductive bias. Ground-truth certification uses GPU-accelerated enumeration, an independent pure-Python reference, and exact cross-checks (byte-for-byte agreement of per-output program counts, witness re-execution, bit-identical posterior agreement). Models are scored with a bounded symmetric divergence against the optimal posterior, summarized by a difficulty-aware score and facet profile across induction, continuation, and abduction tasks.8f:T6cd,The work is a controlled benchmark. The design holds model, harness, task, evaluator, and execution environment fixed within paired blocks, changing only the user prompt. Prompt variants are frozen templates. The primary variants preserve the objective, acceptance criteria, and test command while changing framing: precise baseline, deep thinking, exhaustive exploration, multiple approaches, maximum certainty, adjacent cleanup, no-questions autonomy, bounded efficiency, and related forms. Stress variants intentionally break semantic equivalence through ambiguity, conflicting constraints, irrelevant context, misleading hints, or multi-turn restatement. The metrics separate behavioral work from billing: reasoning tokens, visible output tokens, tool calls, turns, repeated reads/searches/tests, time to first edit, wall time, out-of-scope changes, cached and uncached input tokens, actual cost, and estimated no-cache cost. The main statistic is a paired reasoning ratio against the median baseline for the same model-harness-task block. A prompt is labeled wasteful only if the median ratio exceeds 1.5, the lower confidence bound exceeds 1.1, there is no material success gain, and the effect appears across multiple tasks.90:T764,The setup distinguishes the as-of date t0 from the model training cutoff T. Text written after t0 but before T is bridge data. It can contain information caused by the later world state that also determines the final outcome Y. A model trained on this bridge data may obtain outcome information without ever seeing the benchmark item itself. The paper formalizes this as a back-door leakage path from the later world state through bridge data into the model prediction.

The first technical result is a non-identifiability theorem. A passive backtest observes forecasts, outcomes, timing relative to the cutoff, and possibly covariates, but it cannot separate recency from leakage. The identified set for leakage inflation is a sharp interval, and collecting more items does not make it collapse. A flat pre/post profile is therefore not proof of cleanliness, and a non-flat profile is not proof of leakage.

The second part derives a per-question leakage law. Inflation is the product of honest uncertainty and an extraction factor. The extraction factor has a strong nonlinear payoff: extracting half of the leaked signal already yields about three quarters of the full inflation. This explains why weak recall can still move benchmark scores. The analysis predicts that leakage concentrates on questions that surprised the crowd and had dense training coverage.

The measurement strategy requires an external reference. With a known cutoff, the paper uses a regression-discontinuity design to identify cutoff-localized leakage. With a matched clean control, it uses a difference-in-differences design to estimate global leakage and report a leakage-adjusted score. Matching is central: naive pre/post comparisons are replaced by comparisons that control for timing, question characteristics, and baseline difficulty. Paraphrase probes are treated as detection tools, not measurement tools.91:T4ee,The empirical section starts with ForecastBench. The authors evaluate five flagship models on the official panel, restricted to questions that resolved after each model’s documented training cutoff. These outcomes could not have been memorized under the documented cutoffs. Even so, four of the five models fail the standard pre/post check, with spurious leakage gaps as large as +0.061. A matched-window check collapses the gaps across all five models, supporting the interpretation that the apparent signal is recency rather than leakage.

The estimators are validated using twin models with planted leakage. One model is kept clean, while the other receives controlled leakage. The proposed estimators recover the planted dose, location, and per-question profile, and return a null result on the clean twin. On deployed frontier systems, the estimators identify one cutoff-localized signature and clear five models whose apparent advantages were explained by recency at the design’s power floors.

The most important reported numbers are: five flagship models; four false failures under the standard check on post-cutoff-resolved questions; a maximum spurious gap of +0.061; and successful recovery of planted leakage in controlled twin-model experiments.92:T454,The methodology has three notable layers. It organizes tasks from multiple agent benchmarks into a sequential task stream. After each task, the agent updates an evolution state using its trajectory and self-generated feedback. That state can represent different self-evolution mechanisms: prompt/context refinement, structured memory, reusable skill libraries, or a more integrated harness.

The most important design choice is the three streaming scenarios. In Isolated, each benchmark forms its own stream, so experience is accumulated only within domain. In Sequential, benchmarks are concatenated in a fixed order, so experience transfers from one benchmark to the next. In Interleaved, tasks from all benchmarks are shuffled into a single mixed stream. This is not just a data-order variation. It explicitly controls two variables: the scope of experience transfer and the degree of domain mixing.

The evaluation spans five representative self-evolving methods, ACE, A-Mem, ReasoningBank, AutoSkill, and Harness; three frontier foundation models, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.7; and six agent benchmarks, AppWorld, BFCL, BrowseComp-Plus, HLE, SWE-bench-Verified, and Tau2. The paper is therefore an interaction study across scenario, model, and method, rather than a new algorithm paper.97:T6aa,There are three main findings.

First, self-evolution is not reliably beneficial, and the streaming scenario matters a lot. Isolated is usually the most reliable because the experience distribution is narrower and less contaminated. Sequential is often worse than Interleaved, which is somewhat counterintuitive. The paper’s interpretation is that fixed-order transfer can inject strong domain-specific bias from earlier benchmarks into later ones, causing negative transfer, whereas interleaving keeps the agent exposed to multiple domains and can work better for retrieval-based experience mechanisms.

Second, gains are gated by model capability. The weakest model can show negative evolution gain, meaning self-evolution makes it worse. A mid-capability model can benefit more than a stronger one, so the effect is not monotonic in base-model strength. A reasonable reading is that the model must be strong enough to extract signal from noisy self-generated experience, but once the base model is already very capable, the marginal value of external evolution mechanisms may shrink.

Third, no single self-evolution method dominates across all models and scenarios. Context-integrated methods tend to work better in Isolated streams, while retrieval-based methods are stronger in Interleaved streams. Method choice also depends on the underlying model, so one should not assume that a method that works on one model will transfer cleanly to another.

The paper’s value lies less in any single score and more in the combinatorial structure of the evaluation. It reframes the question from “does this method help on average?” to “under what stream structure and for which model does it help?”98:T664,A fully crossed controlled experiment is used to isolate backend effects, with all nuisance variables held fixed: a single RTX 3090 GPU, fp16 weight precision, and a unified evaluation protocol. - Verbalization-based: prompt the LLM to output a numeric confidence (with variants like CoT/self-probing/top-k verbalization).
- Sampling-based: sample multiple predictions and aggregate (e.g., consistency frequency; mean of sampled verbalized confidences).
- Logit-based: use token log-probabilities (e.g., probability of the class-label token) when the API exposes logprobs.
Main analysis: verbalization yields highly discrete confidence values due to strong preferences for certain numeric tokens, producing only a few distinct thresholds.
Evaluation pitfall: AUARC requires integrating a curve defined by discrete operating points. Linear interpolation effectively invents intermediate operating points, which can over-credit sparse methods; stepwise interpolation better matches the semantics of thresholding (metrics should not change until the threshold crosses an actually attainable confidence value). The authors advocate standardizing stepwise interpolation.
Proposed method: verbalization logprobs. Instead of treating the single generated confidence number as the estimate, it uses the token probabilities (logprobs) of the verbalized digits/values to compute a probability-weighted (continuous) confidence score, reducing sparsity without additional sampling cost (assuming logprobs are available for generated tokens).9b:T788,The method builds a proxy for the “visual direction” using a controlled intervention, then projects the teacher correction onto that direction. During training, the student generates prefixes on the full image x^0. A fixed teacher is queried on the same textual prefix under two training-only views: an evidence-present view x+ and an evidence-removed or degraded view x-. The difference between their centered log-probabilities defines u_t, a signed proxy for how revealing or removing the relevant evidence changes token odds. The sign matters: visual evidence can support some candidates and actively refute others.

VAD then avoids directly matching the privileged teacher distribution. Instead, it starts from the teacher correction relative to the student distribution and extracts the component aligned with u_t through a regularized projection. Intuitively, the teacher may want to move the student in many directions, but only the part consistent with the intervention response is treated as distillable visual correction. The remaining component is kept as an unexplained residual rather than being assumed to be useful supervision. A new target is reconstructed around the student’s current full-image distribution: tokens supported by the intervention are raised, tokens refuted by the intervention are suppressed, and teacher shifts not captured by the proxy are excluded.

Two stabilization choices matter. First, the method keeps a weak regularizer derived from the original teacher correction, so optimization does not rely entirely on a noisy counterfactual proxy. Second, u_t is split into support and refutation branches, allowing separate control over which candidates should be promoted and which should be pushed down. This is a meaningful departure from positive-only visual-advantage weighting. The paper’s central claim is that VAD changes what to distill, not merely how strongly to distill it.9c:T65c,The evaluation uses 4B and 9B students on six fine-grained visual benchmarks. That diagnostic is the empirical basis for the source-mixing claim.

Second, VAD consistently outperforms direct privileged-view distillation and visual-advantage weighting across both model scales and all six benchmarks. The introduction does not expose the full table values, but the paper presents the gains as broad rather than concentrated in one task, which supports the target-reconstruction argument.

If the goal is adaptation or reproduction, then inspect how evidence-present and evidence-removed views are constructed, the cost of the extra teacher queries, and the exact form of the regularization term.9e:T6ac,ObjectStream is a training-free, plug-and-play memory framework built on frozen Video-LLM representations. It does not modify the backbone model. The method has three components.

The first is Latent Object-Anchored Memory. Instead of storing historical visual tokens as a flat sequence, the method induces spatially coherent latent object candidates directly from patch-level features of the frozen model, links corresponding objects across frames, and maintains their histories under a memory budget. The goal is to convert long video memory from token-centric storage into object-centric trajectories.

The second is Object-Conditioned Temporal Residuals. Persistent object histories alone can miss short-lived but important events, such as abrupt appearance changes or interactions. To address that, the method stores residual evidence around object-level changes, preserving transient information that would otherwise be compressed away.

The third is a Recent Visual Grounding Window. Object histories are useful for long-term tracking, but answering current questions still requires access to recent raw visual context. The grounding window keeps the latest observations so the model can remain visually grounded without relying only on abstracted memory.

So the design is a three-part memory system: persistent object histories, transient change residuals, and recent visual context. Compared with token pruning, frame selection, or segment-level memory, the main difference is not just stronger compression but a different organizing principle. The method is also notable for avoiding external detectors or segmentation models; the object-like units are induced from the model’s own latent space.9f:T51b,The experiments cover both online streaming and offline long-video understanding, with Qwen2.5-VL-7B as the main backbone. On streaming benchmarks, ObjectStream improves Real-Time Visual Perception on OVO-Bench by 10.0 points, Backward Tracing by 4.9 points, and StreamingBench by 2.9 points. The gains are especially consistent with the paper’s claim that object-anchored memory helps when evidence must be traced over time.

On offline long-video benchmarks, the method reportedly surpasses the full-token baseline while discarding 82.5% of visual tokens. That is the most important efficiency result: performance is maintained or improved under aggressive token reduction, suggesting that better memory organization can outperform brute-force retention of raw visual tokens.

The ablations support the division of labor among the three components. Object anchors handle long-term consistency, temporal residuals preserve abrupt changes, and the recent window supports immediate grounding. Removing any one of them hurts performance, which indicates that the method is not a single compression trick but a multi-timescale memory design. Since the framework is training-free, the experimental contribution is mainly about showing that frozen models can benefit substantially from better memory structure.a0:T7c6,This is a large empirical analysis rather than a new model. The evaluation is organized as a progression of bias complexity: ImageNet for overall recognition, CelebA for a single spurious attribute, and UrbanCars for two simultaneous spurious attributes. The paper formalizes this through group structure induced by labels and spurious attributes, with the number of groups growing combinatorially as more attributes are involved. That framing matters because it explains why multi-attribute bias is qualitatively harder, not just a slightly noisier benchmark.

The analysis decomposes several design factors: model size, training data size, whether the training data is curated or unfiltered, patch size, and architecture family. A useful part of the paper is that it does not rely only on global correlations. It also performs controlled comparisons where one factor changes while others are kept as comparable as possible within a family. That reduces the risk of attributing gains from better data or newer architectures to scale alone.

Three findings stand out. First, model scaling remains effective for standard recognition but loses predictive power for robustness under complex bias. Second, data properties are more stable: larger and better curated datasets retain meaningful association with worst-group performance even in the harder settings. Third, input granularity matters: coarser visual patches hurt worst-group accuracy, suggesting that fine-grained visual tokens help the model separate causal object evidence from background shortcuts.

The mechanism proposed by the paper is sensible. Contrastive VLM training benefits from frequent image-text co-occurrences, which are often shortcuts. More capacity helps fit those regularities, but does not force the model to rely on causally relevant features. Data curation changes the shortcut distribution directly, and finer patching preserves local evidence that may be necessary to resist background or co-occurrence bias.a1:T5d8,The experimental coverage is the backbone of the paper: 194 public VLMs from 16 families, parameter counts from 63M to 3.6B, and 24 training data sources ranging from 13M to 12.8B samples. The most important numbers are straightforward. The Spearman correlation between model scale and performance drops from 0.68 on ImageNet to 0.48 on CelebA and to 0.05 on UrbanCars. So larger models can become better at exploiting shortcuts rather than better at avoiding them. Data-related factors are more stable: training data size still shows a correlation of 0.41 with robustness on the multi-attribute benchmark, and curated datasets outperform size-matched unfiltered alternatives by up to 25% in worst-group accuracy. The main experimental lesson is not which single model wins, but which design axes keep their effect as the benchmark becomes more bias-sensitive. Same-norm random directions fail to pass 95% paired-difference significance tests on all cells, confirming effective defenses rely on semantically meaningful directions rather than arbitrary perturbation.a4:T417,LUT trains from standard VQA triples. The model first produces a fixed-length continuous latent trajectory and then generates the answer conditioned on the image, question, and latent states. Training has two stages. The first stage, Utility-Aware Latent Distillation SFT, trains a teacher with a visual bottleneck attention mask: answer tokens cannot directly attend to image tokens, and question tokens are also blocked from image tokens to avoid indirect leakage. This forces task-relevant visual information to pass through latent steps. The teacher is trained with answer cross-entropy plus a decorrelation regularizer over final-layer latent states to prevent latent collapse. Candidate trajectories are then scored by information gain, filtered, ordered by utility, and distilled into a student with a low-to-high curriculum. The second stage, LAPO, applies latent attribution policy optimization. It estimates answer-to-latent associations through attention attribution and uses them as step-specific weights during reinforcement learning.a5:Tce6,方法上，作者采用的是一个 decoder-only、Llama-3 风格的统一骨干，并使用 Transfusion 框架把文本的离散 next-token prediction 与图像生成的连续 flow matching 放进同一模型。默认控制实验的主干是 1.5B Llama-like backbone，但由于为 text/image token 设置了 modality-specific split FFN，总参数约 2.3B；大规模验证则使用 13.5B MoE，在 2T token 上训练。文本 tokenizer 使用 Llama-3 BPE，视觉侧支持多种 visual tokenizer，以避免结论只依赖某一种图像离散化方式。

技术贡献可以拆成四块。

第一块是 knowledge flow。作者先在真实数据上看语言、视觉理解、视觉生成之间的迁移，再在严格控制的合成环境里做因果剥离。这里的关键不是简单比较多任务训练是否涨点，而是看哪一种能力会给另一种能力提供可迁移表征，以及这种迁移是否对称。结论是明显不对称：语言对视觉理解、视觉生成的帮助方式不同；视觉生成与视觉理解之间也不是天然互利，而是依赖概念类型。作者用合成数据把概念级 transfer 拆出来，这一点比只在自然图文语料上做 ablation 更干净，因为后者很容易被数据共现和任务难度混淆。

第二块是 synergy vs. competition。作者把“模态是否互相帮助”追到数据复杂度和网络结构两个层面。数据层面，过于复杂的语言或视觉任务会让模态争夺容量；相反，适度简化的一侧可以给另一侧提供辅助监督，形成协同。结构层面，作者分析 Transformer 内部哪些部位更适合共享，哪些部位更适合隔离。结论是 shared attention 更有利于跨模态信息交换，因为注意力负责 token 间路由；而 separate FFN 更适合隔离模态特有变换，减少在参数空间里的直接冲突。这个设计判断很像把 attention 视作通信层，把 FFN 视作模态私有计算层。作者还验证这种现象在不同 visual tokenizer 下都成立，说明不是某个图像表示偶然带来的结果。

第三块是 early unification。作者系统改变视觉数据引入的时间点，以及模态训练的调度方式，比较从一开始 joint training、先文本后视觉、分阶段 curriculum 等方案。核心发现是视觉必须尽早进入，而且要与语言同时共训练。若先把语言模型训得很强，再做视觉接入，模型会出现作者称为 vision laziness 的现象：优化更倾向复用已有语言先验，而不是认真更新视觉相关子网络，导致视觉表征学习不足。这一点对当前很多“先训 LLM、再补视觉”的路线是直接挑战，因为它说明后接视觉不只是效率问题，而是会改变最优解的形态。

第四块是 recipes。作者把前面三类发现合并成可执行 recipe：采用不对称的数据混合比例，使用 shared attention + split FFN 一类的参数共享设计，并坚持早期统一、同步联合训练。然后在大规模 MoE 训练中做单变量对照，验证这些设计在更大参数和更长训练下仍然成立。这里的价值在于，它不是提出一个新模块，而是把多模态预训练里最容易拍脑袋决定的几件事，变成了有实验支撑的默认选择。a6:Ta3c,The model is a decoder-only Llama-3-style backbone trained under the Transfusion framework, where text uses discrete next-token prediction and image generation uses continuous flow matching inside one unified model. The default controlled setup uses a 1.5B Llama-like backbone, but with modality-specific split FFNs the total parameter count is about 2.3B. The large-scale validation uses a 13.5B MoE model trained on 2T tokens. Text uses the Llama-3 BPE tokenizer, and the study supports multiple visual tokenizers so that the conclusions are not tied to one image representation.

The technical contribution is organized into four parts.

1) Knowledge flow. The authors first measure transfer among language, visual understanding, and visual generation on real-world data, then move to synthetic controlled environments to remove confounders. The key point is not just whether multitask training helps, but which capability transfers to which other capability, and whether the transfer is symmetric. Their answer is no: transfer is strongly asymmetric, and the interaction between visual understanding and visual generation is concept-dependent rather than universally positive.

2) Synergy vs. competition. The paper traces modality interaction to both data complexity and network structure. On the data side, simplified tasks in one modality can help the other modality, while high complexity can create competition for capacity. On the architecture side, the authors analyze where sharing helps and where separation is safer. Shared attention appears to support cross-modal routing and communication, while separate FFNs reduce destructive interference by keeping modality-specific transformations private. This is a useful architectural decomposition: attention as the communication layer, FFN as the modality-specialized computation layer.

3) Early unification. The paper varies when vision is introduced and how modalities are scheduled during training. The main result is that vision should be present early and trained jointly with language, not added after a strong language prior has already formed. Late introduction leads to what the authors call “vision laziness”: the model leans on existing language priors and under-optimizes the vision-related components. This is an important challenge to the common retrofit paradigm.

4) Recipes. The final recipe combines asymmetric data mixing, selective parameter sharing such as shared attention plus split FFNs, and early simultaneous multimodal training. The paper then validates these choices with controlled single-variable comparisons at larger scale.a7:T6d1,The experiments operate at two levels. The first level is controlled mechanism analysis. The default model is a 16-layer decoder-only Transformer with hidden size 2048, GQA 32/8, SwiGLU, RoPE, QK-norm, and FlashAttention. The backbone is 1.5B, and the split-FFN multimodal version totals about 2.3B parameters. Using both real and synthetic data, the paper studies transfer among language, visual understanding, and visual generation, then runs systematic ablations over task complexity, parameter sharing, visual tokenizer choice, vision introduction timing, and training schedule. The main findings reported in the text are: transfer is not symmetric; visual understanding and generation interact differently depending on concept type; modality synergy versus competition is largely controlled by data complexity; shared attention plus separate FFNs is a strong structural compromise; and late alignment induces vision laziness.

The second level is large-scale recipe validation. The authors train 13.5B MoE models on 2T tokens and run controlled single-variable comparisons to test whether the earlier findings survive scale. The excerpt provided here does not include all result tables, so exact benchmark numbers are incomplete, but the paper clearly positions the large-scale section as a scaling check rather than a small-model anecdote. When reading the full paper, the most important numbers to extract are: the trade-off curves under different data mixtures; the gains or losses from different sharing patterns such as shared attention versus split FFNs; and the gap between early joint training and late or staged introduction of vision, ideally together with optimization diagnostics that support the vision-laziness interpretation.a8:T641,A good reading order is problem, mechanism, then recipe.

Start with the introduction and section openings to lock in the four claims. The paper is not about standard VLM alignment; it is about unified multimodal pretraining where language, visual understanding, and visual generation are trained together.

Then read Section 3 and Section 5 carefully. Section 3 is the center of the paper because the knowledge-flow analysis motivates the later data-mixing recipe. Pay attention to how real-data experiments and synthetic experiments play different roles: one gives external realism, the other gives cleaner causal interpretation. Do not only look at average scores; check whether transfer is directional and concept-specific. Section 5 matters because it directly informs training strategy. Focus on how the paper defines and diagnoses vision laziness, and whether the evidence comes from gradients, parameter updates, module utilization, or recovery curves.

After that, read Section 4 and Section 6. In Section 4, the most useful takeaway is the shared-attention / separate-FFN design logic. It is worth comparing mentally against alternatives such as full sharing, cross-attention-only fusion, or modality-specific experts. In Section 6, check whether the large-scale MoE results preserve the same trends and whether the single-variable controls are actually clean.

If time is limited, prioritize: the four headline figures, the synthetic knowledge-flow experiments, the early-unification timing comparisons, and the large-scale recipe tables. A careful read should take around 1.5 to 2.5 hours.a9:T79f,The method starts with a single-level discrete wavelet transform. An image is decomposed into one low-frequency approximation band and three high-frequency detail bands. The implementation uses the Haar wavelet throughout, mainly because it is orthogonal, invertible, simple, and effectively acts like a lossless 2×2 average-pooling-plus-residual decomposition. Unlike a learned latent space, this transform introduces no reconstruction loss and requires no extra encoder training.

The core change is not architectural. The model keeps the JiT pixel-space transformer and modifies the noise schedule. The LF band is trained over the full time interval t in [0,1], while the HF bands are only active over [t*,1]. During inference, the model first denoises the coarse band alone. At time t*, HF noise is injected, the bands are recombined through the inverse wavelet transform, and the model continues with joint refinement. This preserves cross-band interaction in the later stage, but avoids spending early trajectory steps on HF content that is effectively pure noise.

Conceptually, this is a frequency-aware flow-matching schedule. Compared with standard pixel-space FM, it explicitly respects the natural frequency hierarchy of images. Compared with latent diffusion, it obtains a coarse-to-fine decomposition without a lossy VAE bottleneck. Compared with progressive multi-scale architectures, it is much simpler and cheaper to integrate into an existing transformer pipeline.

A second contribution is the evaluation protocol. The authors argue that standard FID is too forgiving at high resolution because it downsamples to 299×299 and discards much of the fine detail. They therefore add 5-crop FID for native-resolution local structure and high-frequency Fréchet Wavelet Distance for texture fidelity. This matters because the method is explicitly designed to improve high-frequency generation; using only FID would hide part of the gain.aa:T5b8,The experiments span class-conditional image generation, text-to-image, and video. On ImageNet 512×512, WaiT reports FID 1.43, 5cFID 1.63, and hFWD 0.67, while reducing sampling GFLOPs by up to 50% relative to the JiT baseline. The largest 2B model reaches FID 1.3 on ImageNet 512 for pixel-space models. The paper also highlights that on hFWD, which isolates texture fidelity, WaiT outperforms both pixel-space and latent-space baselines, suggesting the gain is not limited to global structure.

The same trend appears on OpenImages at 512 and 1024 resolution, which is useful because it reduces the chance that the effect is ImageNet-specific. In pixel-space text-to-image at 1024×1024, the method matches or exceeds JiT on almost all metrics while reaching up to 3× higher throughput. With spatiotemporal wavelets, the recipe transfers to video and achieves FVD 0.84 on Kinetics-600.

The most informative evidence comes from the mechanism-oriented analyses. The trajectory visualizations show that HF bands remain nearly indistinguishable from noise early in sampling, which supports the central premise. Ablations around t* expose a quality-efficiency trade-off: delaying HF helps, but the exact delay matters. The three-axis evaluation also reveals disagreement between metrics, with some methods looking strong on FID but weaker on local detail or texture. That strengthens the case that standard FID alone is insufficient for high-resolution generation.ab:T505,This is a skim-level read, but it is worth reading the method and evaluation sections with some care if you work on non-AR generative modeling. Two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. First, frequency bands are only one example of heterogeneous subspaces; the broader issue is whether different parts of the representation should share one corruption schedule at all. Second, the combination of a lossless transform and delayed denoising may transfer to tokenized multimodal generation, where different codebooks or modalities also have mismatched signal-to-noise profiles.ac:T9f3,方法核心是把语音波形先离散成单流 codec token，再在 token 序列上做条件 block discrete diffusion。具体有三层设计。

第一层是表示。作者使用 X-Codec2，而不是传统多码本 RVQ codec。X-Codec2 通过语义编码器和声学编码器融合后，用单阶段 FSQ 量化成单一 token 流，词表大小 6561，帧率 50 Hz。这样每秒约 50 个 token，避免了多 codebook 并行流给 LM 建模带来的复杂性。对 block diffusion 来说，单流离散序列比多流 RVQ 更自然。

第二层是生成目标。作者把长度为 L 的 codec 序列切成连续 block，block size 设为 32，对应约 0.64 秒音频。训练时只对目标 block 内 token 做 masked corruption，mask 概率由连续时间步 t 控制，采用线性日程 α_t = 1 - t。模型输入由两部分拼接：当前被噪声污染的 block，以及之前已经“干净”的历史 block。模型学习在文本条件和说话人条件下恢复当前 block 的原始 token。这个目标继承了 MDLM/BD3-LM 的思路，但这里是条件生成，不是无条件文本 LM。

第三层是注意力结构。作者采用 staircase attention。它不是简单的双向或因果注意力，而是分三种关系：同一目标 block 内双向注意，保证局部声学一致性；当前 noised block 可以看之前 clean block，保证跨块顺序依赖；历史 clean block 内保持因果结构。这个设计的目的很明确：块内需要像填空一样联合恢复，块间又不能完全失去时间顺序。相比 fully parallel diffusion，它更容易维持文本-语音对齐；相比纯 AR，它把一个 block 内的 token 预测并行化，显著降低解码步数。

从全文描述看，条件信息包括文本和 speaker prompt。文本侧应通过编码器或嵌入序列提供跨模态条件，speaker prompt 则提供说话人特征以支持 zero-shot voice cloning。作者强调不使用显式 duration model，这一点很关键，因为很多非 AR TTS 的稳定性来自外部时长约束，而这里希望由 block-wise sequential dependency 自行学出对齐。

如果和已有路线比较：它不同于 VALL-E 一类 AR codec LM，因为预测单位仍是 codec token，但训练目标从 next-token 变成 masked denoising；它也不同于 Voicebox/F5-TTS 这类连续空间 flow matching，因为这里完全在离散 token 空间工作；它和 BD3-LM 的关系最直接，但新增了跨模态条件、说话人条件，以及适配语音局部连续性的 block 设计。ad:T9db,The method has three main pieces.

First, the representation. Instead of a multi-codebook RVQ codec, the model uses X-Codec2, which produces a single stream of discrete tokens via fused semantic and acoustic encoders followed by FSQ quantization. The vocabulary size is 6561 and the frame rate is 50 Hz. This matters because block diffusion is much cleaner on a single token stream than on several parallel codebook streams.

Second, the training objective. A speech token sequence is partitioned into contiguous blocks. The paper uses block size B = 32, which corresponds to about 0.64 seconds at 50 Hz. During training, only the target block is corrupted by masking tokens with probability controlled by a continuous diffusion time t, using a linear schedule alpha_t = 1 - t. The model receives the noised target block together with previous clean blocks, plus text and speaker conditioning, and learns to reconstruct the original tokens in the target block. This is the conditional speech analogue of masked discrete diffusion / BD3-style block denoising, rather than standard next-token prediction.

Third, the attention pattern. The model uses staircase attention. Tokens inside the current target block attend bidirectionally, which supports joint reconstruction and local acoustic consistency. The current noised block can attend to previous clean blocks, which preserves sequential dependencies across time. Previous clean blocks themselves follow causal structure. This is the key architectural choice: within-block prediction behaves like masked infilling, while across blocks the model still respects temporal order. Compared with fully parallel diffusion, this should help alignment. Compared with AR codec LMs, it reduces decoding steps by predicting all tokens in a block in parallel.

Conditioning includes text and a speaker prompt for zero-shot voice transfer. A notable design choice is the absence of explicit duration modeling. The paper is effectively testing whether blockwise sequential dependence plus cross-modal conditioning is enough to learn alignment without an external duration scaffold.

Relative to prior work, it differs from VALL-E style AR codec LMs by replacing next-token prediction with masked denoising over codec tokens; it differs from continuous-space flow/diffusion TTS such as Voicebox or F5-TTS by staying entirely in discrete token space; and it is closest to BD3-LM, but extended to conditional speech generation with speaker conditioning and speech-specific block structure.ae:T5ca,The main reported setup is a 0.6B-parameter model trained on 20K hours of speech. The paper positions this against autoregressive codec LM systems that commonly use 60K to 250K hours, so the claimed data reduction is roughly 3x to 12x. The codec frame rate is 50 Hz and the block size is 32 tokens, or about 0.64 seconds of audio. Inference reaches a real-time factor of 0.15, which is the practical speed result enabled by within-block parallel generation.

On evaluation, the paper highlights competitive intelligibility on the Seed-TTS benchmark and strong zero-shot speaker similarity. The provided text does not include the full result tables, so the exact benchmark numbers are not visible here, but the intended empirical claim is clear: with much less data than large AR baselines, the model remains competitive on intelligibility while being substantially faster.

The most important experimental questions are the mechanism-level ones. The paper attributes gains to three factors: masked diffusion as implicit augmentation, staircase attention for local coherence plus global alignment, and block decomposition for the speed-quality trade-off. If the full paper includes ablations, the critical ones to inspect are: AR vs block diffusion, fully parallel diffusion vs block diffusion, the effect of block size, and whether staircase attention is necessary. The final single architecture supports four core capabilities: 3D understanding, text-to-3D generation, instruction-guided 3D editing, and text-grounded part generation, where part generation is implemented as a standard instruction-following conditional generation task without dedicated pipeline design.b1:T4ef,GROW replaces trajectory-level policy-gradient RL with advantage-weighted flow-matching regression. For each prompt, the current policy samples a group of utterances. Each utterance is scored by two rewards: intelligibility and speaker similarity. Each reward is standardized within the group, then combined into a signed group-relative advantage. This advantage directly reweights the standard flow-matching loss, so samples above the group mean are reinforced and those below it are downweighted. Two design choices matter. First, the group-mean reward baseline turns reward weighting into advantage weighting, which removes prompt-level scale variation and amplifies subtle but meaningful differences among samples from the same prompt. Second, a Wasserstein-2 velocity penalty anchors the updated velocity field to a frozen pretrained reference, limiting drift and helping preserve naturalness. Compared with Flow-GRPO-style methods, GROW keeps deterministic ODE sampling, avoids ODE-to-SDE conversion, and does not require per-step likelihood evaluation. The paper also argues against purely positive exponential weighting: in bounded, tightly clustered TTS rewards, it does not provide enough contrast and can be dominated by the shared imitation component.b2:T433,Experiments are run on LibriSpeech-PC test-clean and the English and Chinese Seed-TTS test sets in a zero-shot setting. The main metrics are WER, speaker similarity, and UTMOS for naturalness. Averaged over the three test sets, GROW reduces WER from 2.016 to 1.558, an absolute drop of 0.458, and increases speaker similarity from 0.676 to 0.715, an absolute gain of 0.039, while keeping UTMOS at roughly the pretrained level. The paper reports that these gains surpass the DiTAR-GRPO baseline overall. On efficiency, GROW with 10-NFE training rollouts reaches performance comparable to its own 32-NFE setting, and is about 2.9× faster to train than the 32-NFE DiTAR-GRPO baseline. At matched training-rollout NFE, GROW is still about 1.1× faster. All final evaluations use 32 NFE to keep inference quality comparable. Ablations cover rollout NFE, CFG, reward weighting variants, and reward composition. The main empirical message is that group-relative advantage works better than naive reward weighting, and the W2 anchor is important for stability and quality retention.b3:T5d3,Proposes JoyAI-Video-Edit, a 16B-parameter autoregressive diffusion framework consisting of an MLLM condition encoder, causal video VAE, and multimodal diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT), supporting instruction-guided V2V and reference-conditioned IV2V editing. The framework is built by first converting a strong bidirectional editor (pretrained via a progressive image and video generation-editing curriculum) into a chunk-wise causal editor, then applying three core techniques: 1) Chunk-wise autoregressive adaptation: bidirectional attention within chunks, causal attention across chunks, a sliding temporal window retaining a fixed number of recent chunks plus the first chunk as a global anchor to bound compute/memory regardless of stream length; training first uses teacher forcing (ground-truth history) then resampling forcing (detached model-generated history) to reduce train-inference mismatch. 2) Source-Anchored Distribution Matching Distillation (SA-DMD): distills multi-step diffusion into a 2-step generator, guides the teacher model along text-conditioning and source-fidelity axes separately, uses temporally aligned source chunks to counteract autoregressive history drift, so the deployed model retains source fidelity with only a single conditional branch. 3) Long-Horizon Autoregressive Distillation: performs segmented optimization over extended rollouts to directly supervise states affected by accumulated autoregressive errors, while keeping training memory bounded.b4:T59e,The central diagnostic tool is a counterfactual sensitivity analysis. Given a problem x and an on-policy trajectory y, every prefix is held fixed and each token y_i is rescored under two opposing privileged conditions: c^pos marks the whole trajectory as correct and c^neg marks it as wrong. The per-token log-likelihood shifts relative to the original policy are denoted z^pos_i and z^neg_i. If shifts truly encoded answer polarity, the two directions should have opposite signs and their magnitudes should distinguish correct from incorrect tokens. Instead, 82%–85% of tokens are insensitive under both conditions at λ=0.05; among jointly sensitive tokens, 91%–96% have the same sign under c^pos and c^neg, indicating that shifts mainly reflect generic reweighting of surface/connector tokens once a final-answer hint is provided, rather than answer polarity. Roughly 58% of the forward-KL optimization magnitude overlaps between opposing conditions, and large-shift tokens are dominated by substitutable surface-form tokens such as “Wait” and “There”. Building on this observation, the paper proposes Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation (CSCR), which uses the difference between the two counterfactual shifts, rather than their absolute magnitude, to measure a token’s true sensitivity to the outcome, and reallocates token-level advantages accordingly, avoiding uniform gradients on non-polar surface tokens.b5:T4d9,SVR makes the model emit, at every turn, a solution, a discrete verdict, and a confidence estimate. The verdict is one of Correct, Incorrect, or Unsure. At inference, the trajectory stops only when the verdict is Correct and the confidence exceeds a threshold; otherwise, the next prompt includes the original problem, the previous solution, and the model’s own self-verification. Correctness labels are used during training to build rewards, but they are never inserted into refinement prompts and are not available to the inference controller. Training uses fixed-horizon trajectories with a GRPO-style objective. Per-turn solve, verification, and format scores are averaged into a trajectory return, while optimization is applied to the final completion tokens rather than treating intermediate turns as separate samples. The confidence reward uses a Brier-style calibration term, penalizes confident mistakes, and encourages recognizing both error states and correct states that are eligible for stopping. Compared with fixed-budget refinement, the main change is not longer reasoning but learned answer retention. Compared with verifier-guided methods, the deployment-time information boundary is reduced to the model’s own outputs.b6:T401,The experiments use Qwen3.5-2B on seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic search, grade-school word problems, competition math, and multi-step reasoning. It improves over the strongest non-oracle multi-turn baseline by 7.5 percentage points and is reported to exceed the evaluated fixed-budget oracle-guided reference by 4.4 points in the complete-system comparison. Fixed-budget sweeps with the same trained policies show that no single shared stopping turn matches adaptive SVR, which supports the claim that the gain comes from instance-level retention rather than simply generating more turns. SVR also matches the aggregate accuracy of 10-sample GRPO majority voting while using roughly half as many tokens. The scope is still bounded: the evidence is mainly mathematical reasoning with a 2B-scale model, so transfer to larger models, code execution tasks, or open-ended generation remains an open question.b7:T501,The "margin cliff" phenomenon is first documented: across 14 unlearning methods spanning gradient-based, preference-based, and distillation-based families, converged unlearned models have per-token answer margins (log-probability gap between the gold token and its strongest competitor) on forget samples that cluster in a narrow band above the retain-only reference model's margin, rather than falling to the reference level. The position of this margin directly predicts how easily content can be recovered via relearn attacks. KKT stationarity analysis shows the cliff arises when the retain regularizer holds the diagnostic log-odds of forget content above a floor, a condition induced by token-saturating losses whose gradients vanish once forget tokens are suppressed. Margin Calibration (MC) is a non-saturating correction: a softplus hinge loss anchored at the reference model's per-token margin, whose gradient scales with the margin gap and thus does not vanish even when forget tokens are suppressed. A KL constraint on a disjoint instruction corpus limits drift on non-forget behavior. For a fixed public task context W=w, the context includes the task, claimed identity, role, and stated use, but these claims are not treated as evidence of actual downstream use. The deployment has a finite release menu A, including refusal. Each release has a utility under a legitimate-use world B and a misuse utility under a malicious-use world M; because the malicious user can choose how to exploit the answer after observing it, the malicious utility takes the most useful allowed misuse. A safeguard is modeled as a Markov kernel over terminal releases conditioned on a pre-release transcript H. The central assumption is that the attacker can reproduce the same observable evidence as a legitimate user. Total variation distance is used to quantify imperfect copying or credential separation. Under a legitimate utility target q, the paper derives a capability floor Γ(q): the unavoidable amount of attacker assistance induced by preserving useful answers. This differs from jailbreak-specific work because it proves a structural lower bound for any safeguard based only on copyable evidence, including randomized decisions and multi-turn verification.ba:T6ca,The method has three main components.

First, policy decomposition. For N rewards, PRISM does not train one policy to maximize all of them jointly. It trains N positive policies, each dedicated to one reward, plus one global negative policy that captures undesirable behavior across rewards. The design choice is deliberate: desirable behavior is often reward-specific, while failure modes can often be pooled under a shared “do not do this” branch.

Second, efficient parameter sharing. PRISM does not instantiate N+1 separate full models. It uses one shared LM and conditions different sub-policies with different prefix tokens. This keeps training and serving practical while preserving a shared representation backbone.

Third, policy composition. At rollout and inference time, PRISM combines sub-policies by taking a weighted sum of their logits, producing a mixture policy. The merge weights become an explicit preference-control interface. Unlike reward weights, these coefficients act on already-optimized policy distributions rather than on raw reward scales, which is the authors’ main argument for improved robustness and interpretability.

Optimization is built on GRPO. Each reward mainly updates its corresponding positive branch, while the negative branch absorbs failure signals across rewards. Relative to linear scalarization, adaptive reward weighting, or constrained/Lagrangian formulations, the novelty is not in the policy-gradient estimator but in moving composition from reward space to policy space. The paper does not deny Pareto trade-offs; it argues that trade-offs are better handled after separate optimization, through policy mixing, than by collapsing all objectives into one scalar during training.bb:T668,The evaluation covers three multi-reward settings: scientific QA, tool use, and helpfulness–safety alignment.

The gains appear on both smaller and stronger instruction-tuned models, though the magnitude varies.

Three necessary conditions for collapse are identified: blanket answering has negative expected score (the exact scenario the penalty rule targets), all prompts share a bounded readout head, and abstention is treated as an action-level choice. It then derives a finite-time collapse law: mean training reward converges to 0 at a 1/t rate (up to log factors) independent of anchor strength β. It further analyzes how advantage estimators modify the law: group normalization steepens decay to 1/t² below an answer rate knee of ~1/G (G = group size) and silently replaces the designed penalty λ with an effective λ_eff=1; dynamic resampling preserves collapse magnitude per rollout. The repair moves abstention out of the action space entirely: during training, the model does not choose to answer or abstain, but is required to output a continuous confidence report trained with a strictly proper scoring rule plus a correctness reward; thresholding for abstention is applied only at deployment. This design eliminates the shared vanishing gradient factor, and the calibrated optimum becomes an interior attracting point.be:T4cb,RSTG first analyzes GRPO, OPD, and SFT under a shared policy-gradient view. GRPO estimates advantages from group rewards; when all rewards in a group are identical, the advantage disappears. OPD minimizes reverse KL from the student to the teacher on student-generated trajectories and can be written as a token-level advantage based on the teacher-student log-probability gap. This dense signal is noisy and asymmetric because many student tokens have low teacher probability, producing mostly negative advantages. RSTG uses three controls. First, sample selection applies OPD only when the student fails and the teacher succeeds, focusing on negative zero-variance prompts and weighting the signal by teacher mastery. The paper reports that using only 3.63% of the full data in this way outperforms standard OPD over all samples. It leaves the base multi-turn rollout pipeline unchanged and requires no additional labels or learned critic. It converts verifier score traces into turn-level advantages via three reference comparisons:
1. Retrospective credit compares each turn's score against the best prior score, capturing immediate progress, success preservation, and regression.
2. Hindsight delayed credit, applied to eligible non-improving turns before success, compares their realized future-best score against eligible trajectories of the same prompt and turn index, identifying turns that lay groundwork for later success without immediate improvement.
3. Fixed-history counterfactual estimation, applied to high-surprisal eligible turns, samples alternative outputs under the same history and compares them to the original output via the verifier, resolving credit ambiguity for high-uncertainty turns.
A fixed-budget training protocol is used: rollouts continue to the maximum turn count even after early success, to observe preservation or regression after correct states are reached. The resulting turn-level advantages are broadcast to all tokens in the corresponding turn and optimized with a clipped GRPO-style objective.c1:T481,The framework treats per-problem failure probability of the policy as a random variable over sampled problem instances. By the Hausdorff moment theorem, a distribution supported on [0,1] is uniquely determined by its full sequence of moments, so single-moment objectives capture only partial information about policy behavior. Multi-Moment Policy Optimization (MMPO) jointly minimizes multiple moments of the failure distribution, an objective that maps operationally to minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to obtain a first correct response, naturally balancing average performance and attention to high-failure hard problems. A generalized moment transformation framework further unifies a broader family of policy optimization objectives—including MaxRL, which is interpreted as optimizing moments of a transformed rather than raw failure distribution—and proves that this family of objectives is strictly Schur-convex, meaning optimization explicitly pushes for more balanced success rates across problems. The practical training surrogate is compatible with existing on-policy RLVR pipelines without major modifications.c2:T40d,The method, HL-Gauss PPO, replaces the scalar MSE value head with a categorical head over a discretized value support. The actor side is unchanged: the categorical distribution is decoded into a scalar expectation, which is then used in standard GAE and PPO updates. This is not a distributional policy-improvement method; classification is used only as a surrogate objective for learning a scalar critic.

The paper includes controls for one-hot and two-hot targets, a Bernoulli two-bin baseline, support choices, and smoothing. These ablations separate several possible explanations: binary classification, extra output-head capacity, target smoothing, and the value-support parameterization. The MSE critic becomes overconfident on prefixes likely to fail and produces asymmetric advantages, while the HL-Gauss critic gives better calibrated scalar predictions and more balanced actor signals.c3:T77e,BiCAA builds a bidirectional process reward. The paper argues that a single process signal is insufficient. Forward-looking rewards encourage locally helpful search, but they do not distinguish necessary steps from redundant ones. Pure hindsight credit can identify pivotal decisions after the fact, but it does not tell the agent whether a step actually improved the information state when it happened. BiCAA combines both.

The first branch is forward solvability gain. For a question with ground-truth answer, each retrieval step is treated as incremental evidence acquisition. At step t, the method compares the model’s conditional log-likelihood of the correct answer given the trajectory prefix up to t versus up to t-1. This marginal change measures whether the newly retrieved evidence makes the answer more solvable. In other words, it is an immediate estimate of how much that search action improved the model’s belief in the correct answer.

The second branch is hindsight success criticality. This branch looks back over the full trajectory and estimates whether a step was actually pivotal for reaching a correct final answer, rather than merely producing a small local gain. The full formula is not visible in the provided excerpt, but the intended role is clear: steps that are causally important to successful trajectories should receive more credit, while accidental or redundant steps should be downweighted.

BiCAA then uses a modulation rule to combine the two signals. A step that both increases local solvability and proves critical in hindsight gets amplified credit. A step with only weak local gain or low retrospective importance gets reduced credit. Finally, the calibrated process reward is fused with the trajectory-level outcome reward through unified advantage estimation for RL updates. The novelty is therefore in reward decomposition and credit shaping, not in a new RL optimizer.c4:T460,From the available full-text excerpt, the experimental story is centered on two outcomes: final answer quality and search behavior quality. The paper claims that BiCAA reduces redundant search behavior and achieves competitive answer performance on multi-step search tasks. Given the method, the most important evidence is not a single benchmark score but process-level analysis: fewer unnecessary search iterations, better search efficiency, more stable training, and less policy collapse compared with vanilla GRPO.

The excerpt does not include the full result tables or exact numbers, so the strongest confirmed conclusion is that combining dense process rewards with outcome rewards works better than outcome-only supervision. The first is task construction. The motivation is straightforward. If training starts only from the composite task, supervision is too sparse to teach which intermediate forms are useful for certificate assembly. The second layer is supervised fine-tuning. Starting from Phi-4-reasoning-plus, they apply assistant-token QLoRA SFT on direct solutions and simulated symbolic traces. This separation is methodologically clean: it tries to teach when and why to use tools, not just how to format a call.

The third layer is verifier-grounded GRPO. The model is further optimized with task-specific symbolic rewards. For weighted-SOS, a terminal candidate is accepted only if it satisfies strict structural constraints: it parses into a finite sum, every weight is an exact positive rational, every summand is a polynomial square, and the expanded identity matches the target polynomial coefficient by coefficient. The key point is that reward is anchored to decidable correctness rather than fuzzy preference signals. Compared with generic math RL, the room for reward hacking is smaller because terminal acceptance is exact.

The main novelty is not a new optimization algorithm. It is the full loop: curriculum-style algebra supervision, simulated traces, native symbolic tools, and exact verifier-based rewards. Unlike many tool-use agent papers, this one deliberately stays inside a fully checkable algebraic domain, which makes it easier to separate tool reliability from strategy failure. The paper is also careful not to overclaim beyond this setting.c6:T80c,The experimental setup is fairly clear. After each rollout, every failed trajectory is sent to a frozen judge (Qwen3.6-27B) together with the gold answer, producing a 1–2 sentence critique of what should have been searched differently. The critique is broadcast as a prefix to a frozen teacher (the student's initialization, also the GRPO KL anchor), whose log-probabilities supply an on-policy distillation (OPD) loss on the student's search-action tokens within failed trajectories. The OPD loss uses a clamp coefficient with a stop-gradient on the teacher-student logprob gap, so gradients flow only on tokens where the teacher is more confident than the student; a lower clamp restricts gradient flow and an upper clamp prevents outliers from dominating. Answer tokens are left to GRPO. Total objective is GRPO + λ_OPD·L_OPD with λ=0.01. The key design choice is that the judge sees the gold answer, making the critique directive rather than evaluative, and post-hoc generation removes the need for an online PRM.c9:T584,CVPO has two components.
(1) Trajectory level: Value-Variance Adaptation. A value model estimates token-level V(s_t) along each generated trajectory. The variance of these values (or a closely related advantage-variance proxy) is used as an intrinsic randomness / exploration indicator: high variance implies more exploratory, low variance implies rigid generation. The paper sketches a bound showing the policy-gradient norm can be upper-bounded by a term involving advantage variance under a bounded ∥∇ log π∥ assumption, motivating variance-aware control of update magnitude. Based on this, CVPO modifies advantage computation by scaling/reweighting trajectories according to their value-variance, with different handling for different reward types (e.g., sparse correctness vs denser rewards), aiming to extract more informative gradients from otherwise homogeneous outcomes.
(2) Prompt level: Dynamic Curriculum Learning. It maintains a moving estimate of prompt difficulty and dynamically reweights/samples prompts to counter difficulty drift, allocating more training budget to prompts that remain challenging at the current stage.
Compared to GRPO, CVPO is explicitly value-based and goes beyond group reward averaging by injecting a variance signal into advantage shaping. 围绕这个概念，RAIL 做了三层设计。

第一，它把 rollout intervention 建模成一个 online contextual bandit。context 是当前任务或轨迹状态，action 是一个结构化 intervention 选择，observed utility 是实际观测到的 recoverability gain。这样做的意义是，controller 学到的是“在当前 policy、当前状态分布下，什么干预最能带来额外学习信号”，而不是依赖固定规则。作者明确把这一步用来弥补 non-stationary gap：policy 在变，干预策略也应跟着学。

第二，action space 不是单一的 rollout 数量，而是 structured intervention space。虽然给出的全文片段没有展开全部细节，但从引言和方法定义看，至少包括在哪里 branch、采用哪种 intervention strategy 等耦合决策。作者把这一步用来弥补 non-scalar gap：很多有价值的干预不是“多采样几个”这么简单，而是要在正确的状态、以正确的方式扩展轨迹。

第三，部署方式采用 shadow-to-live procedure。先用一个短 shadow phase 收集 intervention traces 和 supervision，不直接让 learned controller 影响主训练；等 controller 对 utility 有一定把握后，再进入 utility-gated live phase，选择性地把它接入 policy optimization。这个设计比较务实，因为在线学 intervention policy 容易把训练搞偏，先 shadow 再 live 相当于给 controller 一个冷启动缓冲区，也降低了早期错误干预的代价。

从整体上看，RAIL 不是改 GRPO 的 policy gradient 公式，而是改 rollout generation process。它把 rollout 生成从固定程序变成可学习、可适应的训练环节。和基于 entropy、variance 的启发式 branching 方法相比，差别在于：RAIL 关心的是 intervention 的 realized utility，而不是某个代理指标是否高。d0:T7cf,RAIL stands for Recoverability-Aware Intervention Learning. Its central concept is recoverability, defined as how much an intervention improves the reward-distribution signal at a task or trajectory state. The emphasis is not just on final reward, but on whether the intervention exposes more informative reward contrast for learning.

The method has three main layers.

First, rollout intervention is formulated as an online contextual bandit. The context is the current task or trajectory state, the action is a structured intervention choice, and the observed utility is the realized recoverability gain. This directly addresses the non-stationary gap: as the policy evolves, the intervention policy should also adapt from observed outcomes rather than remain a fixed heuristic.

Second, the action space is structured rather than scalar. From the paper’s framing, it includes coupled decisions such as where to branch and which intervention strategy to apply, not merely how many additional rollouts to generate. This addresses the non-scalar gap: useful intervention often depends on acting at the right state with the right branching pattern, not just increasing sample count.

Third, deployment uses a shadow-to-live procedure. A short shadow phase collects intervention traces and supervision without directly affecting the main optimization loop. Once the controller has enough signal, a utility-gated live phase selectively applies it during policy optimization. This is a practical design choice because online intervention learning can destabilize training if deployed too early; the shadow phase acts as a cold-start buffer.

Overall, RAIL does not modify the GRPO gradient formula itself. It modifies the rollout-generation process, turning it from a fixed procedure into an adaptive, learned component of training. Relative to entropy- or variance-based branching heuristics, the key difference is that RAIL optimizes for realized intervention utility rather than a proxy statistic.d1:T4cf,The paper states that it evaluates RAIL along four axes: effectiveness, adaptivity, expressiveness, and efficiency, and that it outperforms heuristic intervention baselines across multiple benchmarks. However, the provided full-text excerpt does not include the detailed result tables, model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact gains, so those numbers cannot be reproduced reliably here.

What can be inferred from the text is still useful. Second, structured intervention outperforms scalar budget control, supporting the non-scalar argument. Third, the shadow-to-live mechanism is presented as an important stability device rather than a cosmetic engineering detail.

When reading the full paper, the most important experimental checks are: whether recoverability gain correlates consistently with downstream training improvement; how the controller’s decisions evolve over the course of training; and whether the controller overhead is offset by rollout savings relative to heuristic baselines. Expressiveness tells you whether structured actions matter beyond scalar budgets. Efficiency tells you whether the controller overhead is justified.

For implementation, you would need the appendix details on the intervention space, the utility definition, and the online update rule.d3:Ta01,技术上最重要的是实验控制做得很严。作者使用参数化 SCM 生成世界：5 到 12 个节点，图结构在 Erdős–Rényi 与 scale-free 间随机，机制既有线性也有非线性，并用 confounding strength ρ 控制潜在混杂。测试域固定在高混杂 ρ=0.9，并筛出观测相关与因果效应符号相反的三元组，形成标准 Simpson trap。训练数据在线生成，避免固定语料记忆污染。每个样本由 4 条 evidence record 加 1 个 query 组成，evidence type 被系统拆成 obs、int、probe、obs_probe、none。这里 probe 很关键：它不是一般 intervention，而是直接对查询变量 X 做 do(X=v)，并观察所有变量响应，因此最接近回答目标查询所需的局部因果证据。

作者先做 α-mixture 扫描：训练时每个样本以概率 α 来自 interventional distribution，α 从 0 到 1 分六档。结果发现 corrected sign accuracy 没有随 α 单调上升，但 Simpson-slope 的幅度单调增大。于是作者提出 magnitude-direction duality：模型从干预数据里学到了响应强度，却没有学会在冲突证据下翻转方向。

接着，全文真正的主结果来自 evidence-type factor 分析。作者固定训练配方，尤其固定在 α=1.0 的纯干预训练，再在推理时只改变上下文证据类型，比较 pure obs、mixed、pure probes 等条件。结果显示，是否能恢复正确因果方向，主要由上下文里放的是什么证据决定，而且呈现剂量效应：观测证据越多，因果方向越被压制。随后用一组零训练成本的 inference-time intervention 去定位机制：增加 probe 数量不能解除压制；删掉观测记录则立刻恢复正确插值；只保留观测格式 token 但移除观测内容时，压制也会释放。这说明抑制不是训练阶段把能力学坏了，而是推理时被上下文内容门控掉了。作者把这种现象描述为“插值电路一直在参数里，但被上下文关掉”。

另外两个技术点也值得注意。其一，作者专门分析了 probe-based causal evaluation 的噪声地板：即便是完美插值器，单次采样也会有 26% 的符号错误，因此必须做 evidence averaging，否则容易把评测噪声误判成模型缺陷。其二，作者做了 0.93B 规模的 rate-level persistence 检查，以及 CLadder 审计与 sign randomization 分析，发现模型还学到一个正效应先验，而且这个先验有两层结构。这些补充实验让结论不只停留在小模型玩具现象。d4:T433,For pretraining research, the contribution is less about a new model and more about correcting a data-mixture intuition. The paper shows that, at least in this controlled regime, the amount of interventional data in pretraining is not the operative variable for whether the model uses interventional evidence correctly. That matters for anyone thinking about causal pretraining, synthetic data curricula, or “higher-quality evidence” mixtures. A second contribution is conceptual: the bottleneck is not only whether causal evidence exists in training, but also whether the inference context activates or suppresses its use. This shifts attention toward context formatting, evidence composition, and conditional retrieval of learned circuits. Third, the evaluation methodology is unusually clean: online data generation, strict train/val/test world separation, computable causal ground truth, and an explicit analysis of the noise floor in probe-based evaluation. It is a negative result, but one that meaningfully constrains how to think about causal data in pretraining.d5:Ta0c,The technical setup is carefully controlled. Worlds are generated from parametric structural causal models with 5–12 nodes, either Erdős–Rényi or scale-free topology, mixed linear/nonlinear mechanisms, and a confounding-strength parameter rho controlling latent confounding paths. The evaluation domain fixes strong confounding at rho=0.9 and selects triples where observational correlation and causal effect have opposite signs, creating a clean Simpson trap. Training data are generated online, so there is no fixed-corpus memorization issue.

Each sample contains four evidence records plus one query. Evidence types are systematically varied: observational records, generic interventions, direct probes on the queried variable, mixed observation-plus-probe contexts, and no-context cases. The distinction between generic intervention and probe is important. Probe records intervene directly on X, the queried cause, and expose downstream responses, so they are the most task-aligned evidence for answering do(X=x)->Y.

The first analysis sweeps the intervention mixture ratio alpha during training. This falsifies the simple hypothesis that more intervention in pretraining should monotonically improve causal direction. Directional accuracy does not improve monotonically, but the estimated Simpson slope grows in magnitude. The authors interpret this as a magnitude–direction duality.

The stronger result comes from isolating the evidence type present at inference time. With training held fixed, including the alpha=1.0 condition, they vary only the context evidence type and show a contextual dose gradient: more observational evidence in context suppresses correct causal direction more strongly. A set of zero-training-cost inference-time interventions then localizes the mechanism. Increasing probe dose does not rescue the model. Removing observational records immediately restores the latent interpolation ability. Keeping observational-format tokens while removing observational content also releases suppression. This argues that the relevant switch is content-mediated and acts at inference time, not that the model failed to store the causal interpolation circuit during training.

A final methodological contribution is the analysis of probe-evaluation noise. Even a perfect interpolator incurs substantial single-shot sign error, so evidence averaging is necessary. The paper also includes larger-scale persistence checks at 0.93B and CLadder-style audits showing a learned positive-effect prior with layered structure under sign randomization.d6:T761,The main experiments come in five parts. First is the alpha sweep. Using a 25.7M GPT-style decoder with 8 layers, vocab size 41, block size 640, trained for 20k steps with batch size 64 and learning rate 6e-4, the authors vary the intervention fraction alpha across six levels from 0 to 1. Corrected sign accuracy is roughly 0.5/0.3/0.2/0.4/0.4/0.4, showing no monotonic gain from more intervention. In contrast, the Simpson-slope magnitude rises monotonically from 0.169 to 0.384.

Second is the 50-world evidence-type comparison. With training fixed, changing only the inference context shifts mean ratio_true from -0.288 in pure observational context to -0.092 in mixed context and +0.418 in pure probe context. Paired McNemar tests are highly significant, with p-values down to 1.1e-9.

Third is the inference-time mechanism test E1. Doubling the probe dose does not remove suppression. Erasing observational evidence raises ratio_true from about -0.09 to +0.56, close to the probe-only condition. This is strong evidence that the capability exists in the weights but is gated off by context.

Fourth is E5, which studies dose titration and content manipulation. One observational record barely suppresses, two dilute the causal signal, and four effectively capture the directional judgment. If observational-format tokens remain but observational content is removed, suppression disappears. The effect is therefore driven by content, not superficial formatting.

Fifth are robustness checks. The suppression pattern persists at 0.93B scale. The train/validation/test split is done over disjoint world domains, with additional novel-topology evaluation. 真正的创新在于作者如何排除其他解释，并把“判别轴”这个说法做成可检验机制。第一步，先观察 lexical speech round 带来的能力交换：关键词识别大涨，情感识别下滑。第二步，用一个 120 倍更小、但在设计上控制 lexical content 的 prosody corpus（Crema-D）做微调，证明情感能力可以快速恢复，因此不是容量不够。第三步，构造 matched-exposure negative control：用 29,428 条显式提到 emotion 的 mined clips，在相同 recipe 和 exposure 下微调，结果情感几乎不动，说明“caption 里写了情感”并不等于模型会学到情感。第四步，再排除 representational truncation 和 general degradation：前者只能解释一小部分差距，后者通过九任务板证明并不存在普遍退化。最后，作者提出 separability statistic，从语料本身估计某属性是否是区分负样本所必需的轴，并在同一批音频上做结构化干预：只改变语料组织方式，让 emotion 成为必须依赖的判别维度，情感能力就恢复；如果只是提高 caption 相似度而不改变判别需求，则恢复不了。这一步把相关性推进到了因果层面的证据。

和常见做法相比，这篇文章不是再发明一个 loss，也不是改模型容量，而是把预训练数据的“结构”拆成了更细的机制变量：同样的音频、同样的 exposure、甚至 caption 明确写出目标属性，都不足以保证属性进入表示；关键是 batch 内负样本能否在不看该属性的情况下被分开。d9:T735,最关键的结果有四组。第一组，加入 lexical-speech round 后，零样本 keyword spotting 提升 76 个点，而 speech emotion recognition 下降 14 个点。作者用的是 MAEB audio embedding benchmark / mteb 框架下的 SpeechCommands（35-way）和 Ravdess，评测方式都是把音频和类别文本映射到共享空间后做匹配。
